**2.1 Project Description**

The Windfield Creek Wind Farm is a proposed 312 megawatt (MW) utility-scale wind energy generation facility to be located in southwestern Bexar County and eastern Comal County, Texas. The project site encompasses forty-seven (47) separate parcels, consisting of nineteen (19) fee simple parcels (designated Parcels 1 through 19 on the survey) and twenty-eight (28) leased parcels (designated Parcels 20 through 47 on the survey). The total gross acreage of the project site, as computed from the metes and bounds descriptions confirmed by this survey, is approximately 8,832 acres.

Planned improvements for the project include seventy-eight (78) wind turbine generator locations (maximum structure height 590 feet above ground level, or AGL), one operations and maintenance (O&M) building, one project collector substation, a 14.2-mile generation-tie (gen-tie) transmission line corridor connecting the project substation to the regional transmission grid, and approximately sixty-two (62) miles of internal access roads providing construction and operational access to the turbine locations and associated infrastructure.

The Federal Aviation Administration has issued Determinations of No Hazard to Air Navigation for all seventy-eight turbine structures, dated November 12, 2024, under Case Nos. 2024-ASW-12345-OE through 2024-ASW-12422-OE. These determinations are valid until May 12, 2026.

**5.4 Discrepancy Discussion**

Preliminary Title Commitment No. BTA-2024-07831 states total project acreage of approximately 8,412 acres, consisting of 3,780 acres for the fee simple parcels and 4,632 acres for the leased parcels. The survey-computed total is 8,832 gross acres, representing a difference of 420 acres. The fee simple parcel subtotal is consistent between the title commitment and the survey (3,780 acres in both cases). The discrepancy lies entirely in the leased parcel acreage: the title commitment states 4,632 acres for leased parcels, while the sum of individual parcel acreages from the metes and bounds descriptions, as confirmed by this survey, totals 5,052 acres --- a difference of 420 acres.

**Surveyor\'s Observation:** This discrepancy may be attributable to one or more of the following causes: (a) the title commitment may have reported net usable acreage for the leased parcels, excluding public road rights-of-way, exclusion zones, or areas within easement corridors, rather than gross acreage from the metes and bounds descriptions; (b) there may be an arithmetic error or transposition error in the title commitment\'s aggregation of individual parcel acreages; or (c) certain parcels may have been inadvertently omitted from, or double-counted in, the commitment\'s acreage summary. The surveyor computed all acreages directly from the metes and bounds descriptions contained in the recorded instruments without deduction for easements, road rights-of-way, exclusion areas, or other encumbrances.

**Recommendation: This discrepancy should be reconciled with the title company (Oakvale Point Title & Abstract Company, Title Officer Janet Whitmore) and confirmed against the individual recorded instruments prior to closing. The 420-acre difference has potential implications for insured value per-acre calculations, lease economics (including per-acre rent and royalty computations), and the overall project footprint as represented in financing documents. **[Section 7 --- Summary of Conflicts Between Survey and Proposed Improvements]{.underline}**

The following is a consolidated summary of all conflicts identified by this survey between existing conditions, easements, or encumbrances and the proposed project improvements as depicted on the client-provided layout plans. Each conflict is cross-referenced to the detailed discussion in Section 6 and, where applicable, Section 8.

**1. CPS Energy Transmission Line Easement vs. Proposed Turbines T-14 and T-15 (Parcels 5, 6, and 7)**

The existing 100-foot wide CPS Energy electric transmission line easement (Item 10) directly conflicts with proposed turbine locations T-14 (Parcel 6) and T-15 (Parcel 7). Both proposed turbine pad locations fall within the easement corridor --- T-14 is approximately 25 feet inside the northern boundary and T-15 is approximately 40 feet inside the southern boundary. The existing high-voltage transmission line conductors would also present physical clearance conflicts with a 590-foot AGL turbine at either location. Shown on Sheets 6 and 7. *Resolution required: turbine relocation outside the easement corridor, or negotiation with CPS Energy for easement vacation and transmission line relocation.*

**2. FEMA Zone AE vs. Proposed Turbine T-42 (Parcel 40)**

Proposed turbine T-42 is located within the mapped FEMA Zone AE (100-year floodplain) on Parcel 40. The proposed turbine pad center is approximately 120 feet inside the Zone AE boundary. The approximate ground elevation at T-42 (1,038 feet NAVD88) is approximately 4 feet below the mapped Base Flood Elevation (1,042 feet NAVD88). Shown on Sheet 16. *Resolution required: turbine relocation outside Zone AE, application for a Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA) or Letter of Map Revision Based on Fill (LOMR-F), or floodplain development permit with elevation certificate.*

**3. Access Road AR-17 vs. Drainage Easement (Parcel 22)**

Proposed access road AR-17 crosses the 30-foot wide platted drainage easement along the northern boundary of Parcel 22 (Item 15). The crossing location is at approximately the midpoint of the easement run. Shown on Sheet 10. *Resolution required: installation of a culvert or bridge crossing to maintain drainage conveyance, with approval from the drainage easement beneficiaries.*

**4. Access Road AR-8 vs. Water Line Easement (Parcel 13)**

Proposed access road AR-8 crosses the 20-foot wide BWCID No. 10 water line easement on Parcel 13 (Item 39). The easement instrument contains a no-build provision. Shown on Sheet 8. *Resolution required: obtain written approval from Bexar County Water Control & Improvement District No. 10 and install protective steel casing around the water line at the crossing.*

**5. Conservation Easement vs. Proposed Turbines T-65, T-66, and T-67 (Parcel 44)**

Proposed turbine locations T-65, T-66, and T-67 are situated within Parcel 44, which is encumbered in its entirety by a perpetual conservation easement held by the Texas Land Conservancy (Item 51). The conservation easement reportedly prohibits structures exceeding 15 feet in height and restricts land disturbance. Proposed turbines at 590 feet AGL represent a fundamental conflict with the easement terms. Shown on Sheet 18. *Fatal conflict: turbine relocation outside Parcel 44 appears necessary unless the conservation easement can be terminated or modified, which typically requires judicial action and consent of the easement holder.*

**6. Restrictive Covenant vs. Proposed Turbines T-30 and T-31 (Parcels 22 and 23)**

Proposed turbine locations T-30 and T-31 are situated on Parcels 22 and 23, which are subject to a restrictive covenant (Item 14) prohibiting structures exceeding 35 feet in height. Proposed turbines at 590 feet AGL would substantially exceed this restriction. Shown on Sheets 10 and 11. *Resolution required: covenant modification, waiver from the property owners association, or turbine relocation.*

**7. Restrictive Covenant vs. Proposed Turbines T-68 and T-69 (Parcels 45 and 46)**

Proposed turbine locations T-68 and T-69 are situated on Parcels 45 and 46, which are subject to a restrictive covenant (Item 52) limiting permitted uses to \"residential and agricultural buildings.\" Wind turbine generators would not appear to fall within these permitted uses. Shown on Sheets 18 and 19. *Resolution required: covenant modification, judicial determination, or turbine relocation.*

**Surveyor\'s General Note:** The foregoing conflicts are shown on the graphical survey sheets with bold notation and highlighted symbols as depicted in the legend on Sheet 1. Resolution of these conflicts is beyond the scope of this survey and is a matter for the client, the project company, and their respective counsel to address. The surveyor stands available to provide supplemental surveys, staking, or other field services as may be required in connection with conflict resolution efforts.

**[Section 8 --- Additional Survey Findings (Matters Not in Title Commitment)]{.underline}**

The following findings were identified during the field survey and are not reflected in the Schedule B-II exceptions of Preliminary Title Commitment No. BTA-2024-07831. These findings represent matters discovered by the survey that may affect title, use, or development of the project site. Each finding should be reported to the title company for evaluation and potential inclusion as an additional Schedule B-II exception.

**Finding F-1: Unrecorded Gravel Road --- Parcel 17**

An unrecorded gravel road was observed crossing Parcel 17 in a generally east-to-west direction. The road is approximately 18 feet wide, surfaced with compacted gravel and caliche material, and extends from the western boundary of Parcel 17 --- where it connects to a county road (County Road 271) --- to the eastern boundary of Parcel 17, where it continues onto an adjacent ranch parcel that is not part of the Windfield Creek Wind Farm project.

Evidence of regular and ongoing use of this road was observed during the field survey, including the following: recent tire tracks from multiple vehicle types (passenger vehicles, pickup trucks, and heavy trucks consistent with agricultural equipment); a maintained road surface that has been graded and is free of vegetation or encroaching brush; and drainage culverts installed at two low points along the road\'s alignment where it crosses natural drainage swales.

No recorded easement for this road was identified in the Schedule B-II exceptions of the title commitment. The road does not appear on the Bexar County road map maintained by the county engineer\'s office, and inquiry with county road and bridge department personnel confirmed that the road is not maintained by Bexar County. The road is not depicted on any available aerial photography index or historical maps consulted by the surveyor.

This road may constitute evidence of an adverse use claim or prescriptive easement. Under Texas law (Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, Chapter 16), prescriptive easements require at least ten (10) years of continuous, open, notorious, and adverse use. The maintained condition and apparent regular use of this road suggest that such criteria may potentially be met, although the surveyor makes no legal determination regarding prescriptive rights, the duration of use, or the existence or nonexistence of any permissive agreement.

The unrecorded road crosses proposed access road AR-14 at one point (where AR-14 runs in a north-south direction near the center of Parcel 17) and is located approximately 60 feet from proposed turbine location T-22. The road and its full alignment across Parcel 17 are depicted on Sheet 9 of the graphical survey.

This finding is not reflected in Preliminary Title Commitment No. BTA-2024-07831 and should be reported to the title company (Oakvale Point Title & Abstract Company) for evaluation and determination of whether an additional Schedule B-II exception is warranted.

**Finding F-2: Building Encroachment --- Parcel 18**

A metal storage building located on the adjacent parcel to the north of Parcel 18 encroaches onto Parcel 18. The building is approximately 30 feet by 50 feet in plan dimension, of galvanized steel construction on a poured concrete slab foundation, and appears to function as a ranch equipment storage structure. The building encroaches onto Parcel 18 by approximately eight (8) feet along a distance of approximately fifty (50) feet (the full length of the building\'s southern wall). The encroaching portion of the building encompasses approximately 400 square feet of Parcel 18.

The adjacent parcel to the north is owned by Walter Briggs per Bexar County Appraisal District records (Property ID No. 268194). The building appears to be a privately constructed agricultural storage building, with no visible signage or commercial use indicators.

Comparison with available historical aerial imagery (specifically, Bexar County 2014 orthophotography obtained from the Texas Natural Resources Information System) indicates that the building was in place as early as 2014, suggesting it has been present for at least ten (10) to eleven (11) years as of the date of this survey. The building\'s concrete slab foundation extends to the full encroachment line, confirming that the encroachment is structural and not limited to eaves or overhangs.

No recorded easement, license, or other instrument authorizing this encroachment was identified in the title commitment or in a search of Bexar County real property records conducted by the surveyor. Under Texas law, an encroachment in place for more than ten years may give rise to claims of adverse possession or prescriptive rights by the encroaching landowner. The surveyor makes no legal determination on this point and defers to counsel for analysis of the legal implications.

The encroachment is located in the northwestern corner of Parcel 18 and is approximately 350 feet from the nearest proposed improvement (access road AR-15). The encroachment does not directly interfere with any proposed turbine location; the nearest proposed turbine (T-23) is approximately 900 feet to the southeast. The encroachment is depicted on Sheet 9 of the graphical survey with detailed dimensions.

This finding is not reflected in Preliminary Title Commitment No. BTA-2024-07831 and should be reported to the title company (Oakvale Point Title & Abstract Company) for evaluation and determination of whether an additional Schedule B-II exception is warranted.

**Finding F-3: Boundary Discrepancy --- Parcel 39 (Western Boundary)**

As noted in Section 4 (Legal Description Comparisons) above, the western boundary of Parcel 39 as described in the recorded deed (Volume 4498, Page 0145, Official Public Records, Comal County, Texas) does not coincide with the existing fence line along the western boundary of the parcel. The existing fence line, consisting of five-strand barbed wire on cedar posts, is located approximately twelve (12) feet east of the deeded boundary line, as measured perpendicularly from the deed line to the fence. The fence line runs in a generally north-south direction, roughly parallel to the deeded boundary but consistently offset to the east by approximately the same distance along its entire length (approximately 1,200 linear feet).

This twelve-foot offset results in the adjoining property to the west (which is not part of the Windfield Creek Wind Farm project) occupying approximately 0.34 acres of land within the deeded boundary of Parcel 39. The adjoining landowner to the west is identified as Martha E. Kessler per Comal County Appraisal District records.

Survey monuments were not found at three corners of Parcel 39: the northwest corner, the southwest corner, and a re-entrant angle point along the western boundary. At each of these three locations, new monuments consisting of 5/8-inch iron rods with plastic caps stamped \"TLS RPLS 5487\" were set by the surveyor in accordance with the metes and bounds description contained in the recorded deed. The new monuments were set at the positions called for by the deed, not at the fence line positions.

The surveyor recommends that this boundary discrepancy be addressed with the adjoining landowner (Martha E. Kessler or successors). A boundary line agreement executed by the parties and recorded in the Comal County real property records would be the most efficient resolution. Alternatively, if the parties cannot agree, a joint retracement survey with the adjoining landowner\'s participation may be warranted to establish the boundary by mutual consent. If the fence has been treated as the boundary by both parties for more than ten years, an acquiescence argument might also be raised.

Section 10 — Surveyor's Recommendations
Based on the findings of this survey, the undersigned surveyor respectfully submits the following recommendations for action by the client, the project company, the title company, and counsel. These recommendations are provided for informational purposes only and do not constitute legal advice.
1.  CPS Energy Easement Conflict (Turbines T-14 and T-15): Resolve the conflict between the existing CPS Energy 100-foot wide electric transmission line easement and proposed turbine locations T-14 (Parcel 6) and T-15 (Parcel 7). The surveyor recommends that the project team evaluate relocating these two turbines to positions outside the easement corridor. Alternatively, if relocation is not feasible from a wind resource or engineering perspective, negotiation with CPS Energy for vacation or relocation of the easement and existing transmission facilities should be initiated well in advance of construction. The scope and timeline of any such negotiation with a municipally owned utility should be carefully evaluated.
2.  FEMA Zone AE Conflict (Turbine T-42): Address the FEMA Zone AE floodplain conflict at proposed turbine location T-42 (Parcel 40). The surveyor recommends that the project team obtain a formal elevation certificate for the T-42 site and consult with FEMA regarding the feasibility of a Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA) or a Letter of Map Revision Based on Fill (LOMR-F). If the site cannot be removed from the SFHA through a map amendment, either the turbine should be relocated outside Zone AE or a floodplain development permit must be obtained from the local floodplain administrator in compliance with 44 C.F.R. Part 60.
3.  Unrecorded Gravel Road (Parcel 17): Investigate the nature and extent of use of the unrecorded gravel road on Parcel 17 to determine whether an adverse use or prescriptive easement claim exists. The surveyor recommends that counsel conduct inquiry with the adjacent landowner to the east and any other regular users of the road to ascertain whether use has been permissive or adverse. The finding should be reported to Oakvale Point Title & Abstract Company for evaluation and potential inclusion as a Schedule B-II exception.
4.  Building Encroachment (Parcel 18): Address the metal building encroachment from the adjacent Walter Briggs property onto Parcel 18. The surveyor recommends that the project team or counsel contact the adjoining landowner to negotiate either (a) removal of the encroaching portion of the building, (b) execution and recording of an encroachment agreement or license, or (c) purchase of the affected strip. An independent survey or boundary confirmation from the adjoining landowner's surveyor may facilitate resolution.
5.  Acreage Discrepancy: Reconcile the 420-acre discrepancy between the Preliminary Title Commitment's stated total project acreage of 8,412 acres and the survey-computed total of 8,832 acres. The surveyor recommends that Oakvale Point Title & Abstract Company review the individual parcel acreages stated in the leased parcel exception documents against the survey-computed acreages provided in Section 5 of these notes. This reconciliation should be completed prior to closing, as the discrepancy may affect per-acre valuations, lease economics, and representations in the acquisition and financing documents.
6.  Parcel 39 Boundary Discrepancy: Resolve the twelve-foot boundary discrepancy along the western boundary of Parcel 39. The surveyor recommends that the project company or counsel contact the adjoining landowner to the west (Martha E. Kessler per Comal County Appraisal District records) to discuss the discrepancy and pursue a recorded boundary line agreement. While the affected area is remote from proposed improvements, the discrepancy should be resolved to ensure clear title to the full deeded area of Parcel 39.
7.  Water Line Easement Crossing (Parcel 13): Obtain written approval from Bexar County Water Control & Improvement District No. 10 for the proposed access road AR-8 crossing of the 20-foot water line easement on Parcel 13. The district's requirements for protective casing and construction methods should be determined and incorporated into the project's civil engineering design prior to construction.
8.  Drainage Easement Crossing (Parcel 22): Coordinate with the Estates of Windfield Creek Property Owners Association and any other drainage easement beneficiaries regarding the proposed AR-17 crossing of the 30-foot platted drainage easement on Parcel 22. Design of the crossing should include a culvert or bridge structure sized to maintain the drainage capacity of the existing channel.
9.  Restrictive Covenants and Conservation Easement: Counsel should evaluate the impact of the restrictive covenants referenced in Items 14, 51, and 52 of the title commitment on the proposed turbine locations identified in this survey. In particular, the conservation easement on Parcel 44 (Item 51) presents what appears to be a fatal conflict with turbines T-65, T-66, and T-67, and the restrictive covenants on Parcels 22/23 (Item 14) and Parcels 45/46 (Item 52) present significant conflicts with turbines T-30, T-31, T-68, and T-69. Modification, waiver, or termination of these instruments — or relocation of the affected turbines — should be addressed as a priority matter in the title due diligence process.

Section 1: Affiant Identification and Authority

TERRAVISTA LAND SURVEYORS LLC 3100 FM 725, Suite B | New Braunfels, TX 78130

David Okonkwo, Associate Holloway, Bates & Fenn LLP 700 Louisiana Street, Suite 3400 Houston, TX 77002

Job No.: TLS-2025-0294 Client: Ridgeline Power Holdings LLC Project Company: Windfield Creek Energy LLC Counties: Bexar and Comal Counties, Texas Title Commitment: Oakvale Point Title & Abstract Company, Commitment No. BTA-2024-07831, effective April 1, 2025 Title Officer: Janet Whitmore
Note: The effective date of the final title commitment (April 1, 2025) post-dates the survey certificate date of March 28, 2025. During fieldwork and survey compilation, this office relied upon a preliminary version of the title commitment bearing an effective date of November 15, 2024, which was provided to our office by Oakvale Point Title & Abstract Company. Counsel should cross-reference the final commitment against the preliminary version to confirm that no additional Schedule B-II exceptions have been added or modified subsequent to the date of our review.
1. Transmittal and Scope of Survey
Dear Mr. Okonkwo:
We are pleased to transmit herewith the completed ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey for the above-referenced project, consisting of twenty-three (23) survey sheets, dated March 28, 2025 (the "Survey"). The Survey has been prepared in full compliance with the 2021 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for ALTA/NSPS Land Title Surveys, jointly established by the American Land Title Association and the National Society of Professional Surveyors, including the accuracy standards set forth therein.
This Survey was commissioned by Ridgeline Power Holdings LLC ("Client") in connection with the proposed acquisition of one hundred percent (100%) of the membership interests in Windfield Creek Energy LLC, the project company holding fee and leasehold interests in the real property that constitutes the Windfield Creek Wind Farm Project (the "Project").
The scope of the Survey encompasses forty-seven (47) parcels comprising approximately 8,832 gross acres (per surveyed metes and bounds computations and field measurements) situated across southwestern Bexar County and eastern Comal County, Texas. The parcels are categorized as follows:
•  Fee Simple Parcels: Parcels 1 through 19, totaling approximately 3,780 acres; and
•  Leased Parcels: Parcels 20 through 47, totaling approximately 5,052 acres, held pursuant to various wind energy lease agreements and memoranda of lease recorded in the Official Public Records of Bexar and Comal Counties.
The following planned improvements were referenced during the Survey, as provided to our office by the Project development team and overlaid onto the Survey sheets for spatial analysis:
•  Seventy-eight (78) turbine locations (maximum structure height of 590 feet above ground level);
•  Operations and Maintenance (O&M) building;
•  Project substation;
•  A 14.2-mile generation-tie (gen-tie) transmission line corridor; and
•  Approximately 62 miles of internal access roads.
The Survey was performed in conjunction with a systematic review of the Schedule B-II exceptions (Items 1 through 63) from the preliminary title commitment, with all locatable easements, encumbrances, and other survey-visible matters plotted on the survey sheets. The following Table A optional items were included in the Survey as requested by the Client: Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6(a), 6(b), 7(a), 7(b)(1), 8, 9, 10, 11(a), 11(b), 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, and 19.
Fieldwork was conducted between January 6, 2025 and March 22, 2025. Our field crews deployed a combination of Global Positioning System (GPS) survey-grade receivers and conventional total-station methods. All forty-seven parcels were physically accessed and traversed during the fieldwork period. Control points were established and tied to the Texas Coordinate Reference System, South Central Zone (NAD83/2011 epoch), and all elevations reference NAVD88 datum.
Acreage Discrepancy Note: We draw counsel's attention to the fact that the gross surveyed acreage for all forty-seven parcels totals approximately 8,832 acres, whereas the title commitment (Schedule A) references a total project area of approximately 8,412 acres — a discrepancy of approximately 420 acres. This discrepancy is attributable entirely to the leased parcels, where the surveyed total is 5,052 acres compared to the commitment's stated 4,632 acres. The fee parcel acreages (3,780 acres) are consistent between the Survey and the title commitment. Our surveyed acreages are computed from the record metes-and-bounds descriptions and confirmed by field measurements, and we believe them to be accurate. We recommend that counsel reconcile these figures with the title company prior to closing. Further detail on this discrepancy is provided in Section 8 below.
2. Summary of Schedule B-II Exception Cross-References
Our office reviewed all sixty-three (63) Schedule B-II exceptions listed in the preliminary title commitment and plotted all locatable easements, encumbrances, and encroachments on the applicable survey sheets. The majority of recorded easements — including utility, road, water line, and electric distribution easements — were located in the field and plotted on the Survey without identified material conflicts with the planned Project improvements.
The following categories of exceptions were located and shown on the Survey without material conflict:
TxDOT Right-of-Way for FM Road 1560 (Item 17). Standard 80-foot right-of-way from centerline, affecting the eastern boundary of Parcels 1, 2, 3, and 14. The right-of-way boundaries were confirmed by existing TxDOT monuments and were plotted in their entirety. No planned turbine locations or internal access roads encroach upon or conflict with the FM 1560 right-of-way.
AT&T Fiber Optic Cable Easement (Item 34). A 15-foot wide easement running along the eastern boundary of Parcel 14. Existing surface markers and a warning tape were confirmed in the field. No conflict with any planned Project improvements.
Bandera Electric Cooperative Distribution Line Easements (Item 18). A 30-foot wide easement traversing Parcels 10, 11, 14, 15, 29, 30, and 31. Existing 7.2 kV overhead distribution lines were confirmed to be located within the designated easement corridors on all affected parcels. No turbine locations are planned within these easement corridors, and no material conflict was identified.
Water Well Easement on Parcel 9 (Item 16). A 25-foot radius easement surrounding an existing water well. The well was located in the field and its buffer plotted on the Survey. No planned improvements fall within this easement area.
Underground Water Line Easements (Items 36–42). A 20-foot wide easement corridor affecting portions of Parcels 2, 5, 9, 13, 17, 19, and 21. All easement corridors were located and plotted based on record descriptions and surface evidence. We note that proposed access road AR-8 crosses the water line easement on Parcel 13 in one location. This is considered a minor conflict requiring coordination with the easement holder during construction but is not a material impediment to Project development.
Private Ranch Road Easements (Items 43–50). A 30-foot wide easement corridor for each of several existing private ranch roads across various parcels. All roads were confirmed in the field and plotted. No material conflicts with planned improvements were identified.
Miscellaneous Utility Easements (Items 55–58). Easements ranging from 10 to 15 feet in width for various utility purposes. All were located and plotted. No conflicts with planned improvements were identified.
Pipeline Easement (Item 11). A 50-foot wide easement traversing Parcel 12 for an active 12-inch natural gas pipeline. The pipeline was confirmed in the field by surface markers, warning signs, and electronic pipe locator. The recorded easement instrument prohibits any construction, grading, or placement of structures within the easement corridor. No turbine locations are planned within this easement. However, access road routing in the vicinity of Parcel 12 should account for the pipeline corridor restrictions.
Drainage Easement on Parcels 22 and 23 (Item 15). A 30-foot wide drainage easement along the northern boundary of Parcel 22 and the southern boundary of Parcel 23. The Survey shows that proposed access road AR-17 crosses this drainage easement in one location. This is considered a minor conflict; construction of any road improvements within the drainage easement will require coordination with the easement holder and potentially Bexar County Flood Control.
Cemetery on Parcel 11 (Item 35). A historic family cemetery was located on Parcel 11 as noted in the title commitment. The cemetery encompasses approximately 0.25 acres, is bounded by a stone wall, and contains approximately twenty (20) visible grave markers. A 50-foot buffer was plotted on the Survey. This cemetery is subject to the protections of the Texas Health and Safety Code, Chapter 711, including requirements for access and preservation. No planned improvements conflict with the cemetery or its buffer.
The remaining Schedule B-II exceptions are either non-locatable by survey methods (e.g., tax liens, ad valorem tax reservations, mineral reservations, regulatory requirements, and general exceptions) or are addressed in the conflict summary in Sections 3 through 8 below.
3. Critical Conflict: CPS Energy Transmission Easement vs. Turbine Locations T-14 and T-15
This section addresses a critical conflict identified between a recorded electric transmission line easement and two proposed turbine locations. This finding requires immediate attention by counsel and the Project development team.
Schedule B-II Item 10 references an Electric Transmission Line Easement dated March 3, 2019, granted by Harold and Mabel Sturbridge to CPS Energy, recorded in Volume 16987, Page 0445, Official Public Records, Bexar County, Texas. The easement is one hundred (100) feet in width and traverses Parcels 5, 6, and 7 in a generally northeast-to-southwest direction across approximately 4,200 linear feet of Project land.
The Survey confirms the existence of active CPS Energy transmission facilities within the easement corridor, including steel lattice towers estimated at 80 to 100 feet in height, carrying high-voltage transmission lines. The easement boundaries were retraced in the field based on the metes and bounds description contained in the recorded instrument and were plotted on the Survey. The proposed turbine layout, as provided to our office by the Project developer, was overlaid onto the surveyed easement boundaries for spatial conflict analysis.
Finding: Proposed turbine location T-14, situated on Parcel 6, is located approximately 35 feet inside the southern boundary of the 100-foot CPS Energy easement corridor. Proposed turbine location T-15, situated on Parcel 7, is located approximately 60 feet inside the northern boundary of the same easement corridor. In both instances, the turbine foundations, crane pads, and rotor sweep zones would fall wholly or partially within the easement area. This constitutes a direct and material conflict between the proposed Project improvements and the recorded easement.
The recorded easement document grants CPS Energy exclusive use rights within the corridor for transmission line construction, operation, maintenance, and repair purposes and expressly prohibits the placement of any structures, buildings, obstructions, or improvements that could interfere with the operation and maintenance of the transmission facilities. The presence of the existing high-voltage transmission infrastructure within the corridor underscores the practical significance of this prohibition.
Recommendation: We recommend that counsel evaluate whether the turbine layout can be modified to relocate T-14 and T-15 to positions outside the CPS Energy easement corridor. Alternatively, counsel should assess the feasibility of negotiating a vacation, relocation, or modification of the CPS Energy easement with CPS Energy. Given the existing high-voltage transmission infrastructure, relocation of the CPS Energy transmission line would be a significant engineering and financial undertaking and would likely require extended coordination with the utility. This finding is depicted graphically on Survey Sheets 7 and 8.
4. Flood Zone Findings: FEMA Zone AE and Turbine T-42
This section addresses flood zone findings identified during the Survey that affect planned Project improvements, specifically proposed turbine location T-42.
In connection with Schedule B-II Item 33 and as part of Table A Item 18, the Survey plotted the FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area boundaries as depicted on FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) Panel No. 48029C0740G, bearing an effective date of June 2, 2021. The Special Flood Hazard Area designated as Zone AE (corresponding to the 100-year floodplain with base flood elevations determined) was identified as affecting portions of the Project site.
The affected parcels are as follows: portions of Parcel 15 and Parcel 16 in Bexar County, and a portion of Parcel 40 in Comal County, are situated within Zone AE. The total area within Zone AE and within the Project boundaries is approximately 87 acres.
Critical Finding: Proposed turbine location T-42, situated on Parcel 40, is located approximately 120 feet inside the mapped Zone AE boundary. The turbine pad, foundation, and crane staging area would all fall within the designated 100-year floodplain. The Base Flood Elevation (BFE) in the vicinity of T-42 is depicted on the FIRM panel at approximately 1,042 feet NAVD88. The surveyed ground elevation at the T-42 pad location is approximately 1,038 feet NAVD88 — that is, approximately four (4) feet below the BFE. This elevation differential confirms that the T-42 location is not only within the mapped flood zone boundary but is situated at an elevation that would be inundated during a 100-year flood event.
With respect to the remaining flood zone areas, the Zone AE designations affecting Parcels 15 and 16 do not conflict with any proposed turbine locations. Minor portions of planned access roads cross the flood zone boundaries on these parcels, and these areas are noted on the applicable survey sheets for informational purposes. No material development impediment is anticipated for the access road crossings, although floodplain development permits may be required.
Recommendation: We recommend that counsel and the development team evaluate the following options: (1) obtaining a Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA) or Letter of Map Revision Based on Fill (LOMR-F) from FEMA if the site at T-42 can be demonstrated to be above the BFE through the placement of fill or through an elevation certification showing the natural ground is above the BFE at the precise pad location (though current survey data suggest the ground is below BFE); (2) relocating turbine T-42 to a position on Parcel 40 that is outside the Zone AE boundary; or (3) securing flood insurance coverage and elevation certificates as may be required by the Project lender and applicable floodplain management regulations. Project lenders typically require that improvements situated within Zone AE carry flood insurance in compliance with the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and applicable federal lending regulations. This finding is depicted graphically on Survey Sheets 15 and 16.
5. Unrecorded Gravel Road on Parcel 17 — Potential Prescriptive Easement
This section addresses a survey-only discovery that is not referenced in any Schedule B-II exception of the title commitment.
During fieldwork on Parcel 17, the survey crew identified an unrecorded gravel road approximately 18 feet wide, running in a roughly east-west direction across the central portion of the parcel for a distance of approximately 1,450 linear feet. The road connects the paved county road along the eastern boundary of Parcel 17 to an adjacent ranch property located to the west, which is not included within the Project site. The road terminates at a cattle guard at the western property boundary line.
Evidence of regular and ongoing use was observed, including fresh tire tracks, a well-maintained gravel surface with evidence of recent grading, and the aforementioned cattle guard in functional condition. Our office reviewed historical aerial imagery from 2012, 2015, 2019, and 2023 vintages, all of which show the road in substantially the same alignment and condition, indicating continuous existence and apparent use for at least twelve (12) to fifteen (15) years. No recorded easement, license, right-of-way, or other instrument of authorization was found in the title commitment that corresponds to this road.
We note that under Texas law, a prescriptive easement may arise where there has been ten (10) or more years of continuous, open, notorious, and adverse use of another's property. See Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 16.026 and applicable case law. The duration and character of the observed use of this road may be sufficient to support a prescriptive easement claim by the adjacent landowner.
Recommendation: We recommend that counsel investigate the nature and history of the road use, specifically whether the use has been permissive (i.e., with the consent of the fee owner of Parcel 17) or adverse. If the use has been permissive, a formal license revocation or termination may be appropriate. If the use is determined to be adverse, counsel should consider obtaining a quitclaim deed, formal release, or easement agreement from the adjacent landowner to resolve the matter of record. The road crosses the planned alignment of access road AR-12, and any unresolved claim to the road could create an impediment to access road construction and title insurance coverage. This finding is depicted on Survey Sheet 12.
6. Building Encroachment onto Parcel 18
This section addresses an additional survey-only discovery not referenced in the Schedule B-II exceptions.
During the boundary survey and physical inspection of Parcel 18, the survey crew identified a metal storage building situated on the adjacent property to the north of Parcel 18 that encroaches across the northern boundary line of Parcel 18. The building is a pre-engineered metal structure on a concrete slab foundation, measuring approximately 24 feet by 40 feet. The adjacent property to the north is owned by Walter Briggs, according to current Bexar County Appraisal District records reviewed by our office.
The encroachment extends approximately 8 feet south of the surveyed northern boundary line of Parcel 18, creating an encroachment area of approximately 8 feet by 40 feet, or approximately 320 square feet. The encroachment was measured from the surveyed boundary line monuments and confirmed by multiple field observations. Based on a comparison of historical aerial imagery from 2012 and 2015 vintages, the building appears to have been in place for more than ten (10) years, with construction likely occurring between 2010 and 2012. The concrete slab foundation extends to the full extent of the encroachment.
No recorded encroachment agreement, license, consent, or boundary line agreement was identified in the title commitment. Under Texas adverse possession statutes (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code §§ 16.024–16.026), ten (10) years of continuous, open, and adverse possession under claim of right may ripen into a title claim. The presence of a permanent concrete slab foundation constitutes a physical occupation of the encroached-upon portion of Parcel 18 that is not easily remedied by mere removal of the surface structure.
The encroachment does not conflict with any planned turbine location, access road, or other proposed Project improvement. However, the encroachment constitutes a title defect and physical encumbrance on Parcel 18 that should be resolved to satisfy lender and title insurance requirements.
Recommendation: We recommend that counsel contact the adjacent landowner, Walter Briggs, to negotiate one of the following resolutions: (a) removal of the encroaching structure and restoration of the boundary line; (b) execution of a recorded encroachment agreement or license specifying the permitted encroachment and its limitations; or (c) a boundary line agreement or lot-line adjustment formalized by a recorded instrument and a revised survey plat. A boundary line survey of the adjacent Briggs property may also be warranted. This finding is depicted on Survey Sheet 13.
7. Boundary Discrepancy on Parcel 39
During the monumentation and boundary retracement of Parcel 39, a leased parcel situated in Comal County and held by Comal Ranch LLC, the survey crew found that permanent monuments were missing at three (3) corners of the parcel — specifically, the northwest corner, the southwest corner, and a re-entrant angle point along the western boundary. New iron rod monuments with aluminum caps stamped "TERRAVISTA RPLS 5487" were placed at these locations based on the metes and bounds description contained in the deed of record (recorded in Volume 3421, Page 188, Official Public Records, Comal County, Texas).
However, during this retracement, the survey crew observed that the existing fence line along the western boundary of Parcel 39, which serves as the physical demarcation between the Project parcel and an adjacent parcel not included within the Project site, is located approximately 12 feet east of the surveyed record boundary line. This discrepancy is consistent along substantially the entire length of the western boundary, a distance of approximately 2,100 linear feet, creating a strip of land approximately 12 feet in width and encompassing approximately 0.58 acres where the existing fence and the record boundary line do not coincide. The adjacent landowner to the west appears to be occupying and fencing this 12-foot strip as part of the adjacent property.
The fence is a five-strand barbed wire fence in good condition, with cedar posts and steel T-posts, suggesting regular maintenance. Our review of historical aerial imagery indicates the fence has been in substantially this location since at least 2012, although we cannot determine the original date of fence construction.
Recommendation: We recommend that counsel and the title company investigate whether the adjacent landowner has any claim to the 12-foot strip — whether by acquiescence, boundary agreement, or adverse possession — and whether a recorded boundary line agreement should be pursued to resolve the discrepancy. This matter does not constitute a critical conflict for turbine placement, as no turbine locations are planned within 200 feet of the western boundary of Parcel 39. Nonetheless, the boundary discrepancy should be resolved to satisfy lender survey review requirements and to ensure accurate title insurance coverage for the leased parcel area. This matter is depicted on Survey Sheet 18.
8. Acreage Reconciliation Note
As noted in Section 1 above, the gross surveyed acreage for all forty-seven (47) Project parcels totals approximately 8,832 acres, computed from the record metes and bounds descriptions and confirmed by field measurements. The acreage figures for the two parcel categories are summarized below:

Our office has verified the individual parcel acreages against the recorded deeds, recorded memoranda of lease, and field measurements. The surveyed acreages for each individual leased parcel are consistent with the acreage figures that can be computed from the metes and bounds descriptions contained in the respective instruments of record. We are therefore confident in the accuracy of the 5,052-acre figure for the leased parcels and the 8,832-acre figure for the total Project area.
We offer the following possible explanations for the discrepancy: (a) the title commitment may be referencing a "net usable acreage" figure that excludes road rights-of-way, exclusion areas, setback zones, or other deducted areas; (b) certain leased parcels may have been omitted or their acreage understated in the preparation of the commitment; or (c) the discrepancy may result from a computational or typographical error in the commitment.
Recommendation: We strongly recommend that counsel and the title company reconcile the acreage figures before closing. The surveyed acreages should be utilized for lease payment verification, insured amount calculations, and all project-related acreage-dependent computations. If the title commitment is revised to reflect the surveyed acreages, the title company should issue an updated Schedule A reflecting the corrected total.

As noted in Section 4 (Legal Description Comparisons) above, the western boundary of Parcel 39 as described in the recorded deed (Volume 4498, Page 0145, Official Public Records, Comal County, Texas) does not coincide with the existing fence line along the western boundary of the parcel. The existing fence line, consisting of five-strand barbed wire on cedar posts, is located approximately twelve (12) feet east of the deeded boundary line, as measured perpendicularly from the deed line to the fence. The fence line runs in a generally north-south direction, roughly parallel to the deeded boundary but consistently offset to the east by approximately the same distance along its entire length (approximately 1,200 linear feet).
This twelve-foot offset results in the adjoining property to the west (which is not part of the Windfield Creek Wind Farm project) occupying approximately 0.34 acres of land within the deeded boundary of Parcel 39. The adjoining landowner to the west is identified as Martha E. Kessler per Comal County Appraisal District records.
Survey monuments were not found at three corners of Parcel 39: the northwest corner, the southwest corner, and a re-entrant angle point along the western boundary. At each of these three locations, new monuments consisting of 5/8-inch iron rods with plastic caps stamped "TLS RPLS 5487" were set by the surveyor in accordance with the metes and bounds description contained in the recorded deed. The new monuments were set at the positions called for by the deed, not at the fence line positions.
The surveyor recommends that this boundary discrepancy be addressed with the adjoining landowner (Martha E. Kessler or successors). A boundary line agreement executed by the parties and recorded in the Comal County real property records would be the most efficient resolution. h1("Executive Summary","1")

h2("1.1  Purpose and principal conclusions")
para("This report summarises and tests the encumbrance package for the acquisition by Ridgeline Power Holdings LLC (the \u201cBuyer\u201d) of 100% of the "
     "membership interests in Windfield Creek Energy LLC (the \u201cProject Company\u201d) from Lone Prairie Renewables Inc. (the \u201cSeller\u201d). It is based on "
     "five documents: a 63-item preliminary title commitment, an ALTA/NSPS survey narrative with certification, a nine-lease surface lease schedule, "
     "a seller's affidavit of title, and the surveyor's cover letter. Each has been read in full, every stated total and date interval has been "
     "recomputed, and each document has been tested against the other four.")

para("The record-title burden on the fee parcels is, in most respects, ordinary for a Texas wind project: utility, pipeline, road, drainage and "
     "water-line easements, tract mineral severances, and standard printed exceptions. Individually, none of those defeats the project. The risk in "
     "this transaction lies elsewhere — in five clusters:")

numitem("**Seller-level liabilities that reach the asset being sold.** A UCC-1 and deed of trust ($9.83 million payoff), an IRS federal tax lien "
        "($523,180), an abstract of judgment ($387,450), a mechanic's lien ($214,800) and delinquent 2024 ad valorem taxes ($1,246,088 before "
        "penalties). The judgment and the federal tax lien are against the Seller, not the Project Company, and therefore do not attach to the "
        "land (Commitment, Items 29 and 32) — but the asset being purchased is the membership interest that those liens can reach. See Sections 5.1 and 10.","(i)")
numitem("**Four priority and land-use problems that constrain siting or tenure.** A perpetual conservation easement prohibiting structures over "
        "15 feet on Parcel 44 (Item 51); a perpetual covenant prohibiting structures over 35 feet on Parcels 22 and 23 (Item 14); a covenant "
        "restricting Parcels 45 and 46 to residential and agricultural uses until November 2, 2040 (Item 52); and a senior deed of trust on "
        "Parcels 33–39 ($2,415,000 outstanding) recorded before the surface lease, with no SNDA obtained (Items 24 and 53; B-I Item 8).","(ii)")
numitem("**A live challenge to 640 acres of the leasehold.** The lis pendens recorded March 5, 2025 in Cause No. 2025-CI-03221 alleges that the "
        "Parcel 20 lease was executed without authority and that a community property agreement was forged. The affected Sturbridge parcels "
        "(20–23) are also the parcels that cannot be reconciled on acreage and that have no Schedule B-II lease-memorandum item. See Sections 5.2, 5.3 and 4.4.","(iii)")
numitem("**Acreage that no document reconciles.** One stated total is 8,412 acres; another is 8,832 acres; the underlying schedules sum to "
        "9,232, 9,234 and 9,252 acres respectively. Each of four documents states \"5,052\" leased acres, yet none of their own line items sums to "
        "5,052. See Section 4 — this is the most significant analytical finding in the report.","(iv)")
numitem("**A seller affidavit that is contradicted by the other documents at nine specific points.** It also refers to a survey prepared by a "
        "different firm bearing a different date, misstates the deed types and acquisition period, omits every monetary lien and the lis pendens "
        "from what it calls a complete accounting, and is not properly acknowledged. See Section 7.","(v)")

para("Two further structural points belong at the front of any report to Buyer. First, the commitment proposes to insure **Ridgeline Power "
     "Holdings LLC as owner** of estates that remain vested in the Project Company, and Schedule B-I Item 2 proposes to create that estate by "
     "assignment of membership interests — which cannot convey real property. Second, the commitment is **unexecuted** in the copy produced, and "
     "under its own terms is not binding until countersigned. See Section 3.")

para("The transaction is not, on the present record, in a condition to close. That is a timing conclusion, not a valuation one: most of what stands "

bullet("**Amendment of Schedule A** to name Windfield Creek Energy LLC as Proposed Insured (or a documented post-closing merger), and withdrawal or restatement of B-I Item 2 (Section 3.3).")
bullet("**Payoff and release** of the Great Plains National Bank deed of trust and termination of the UCC-1 from closing proceeds (Items 8, 9).")
bullet("**Recorded releases** of the GeoTech mechanic's lien (Item 31), the Steelform abstract of judgment (Item 29) and the IRS federal tax lien (Item 32), or an escrow holdback not less than 150% of each amount plus a title company indemnity acceptable to Buyer (Section 9).")

h2("1.1  Purpose and principal conclusions")
para("This report summarises and tests the encumbrance package for the acquisition by Ridgeline Power Holdings LLC (the \u201cBuyer\u201d) of 100% of the "
     "membership interests in Windfield Creek Energy LLC (the \u201cProject Company\u201d) from Lone Prairie Renewables Inc. (the \u201cSeller\u201d). It is based on "
     "five documents: a 63-item preliminary title commitment, an ALTA/NSPS survey narrative with certification, a nine-lease surface lease schedule, "
     "a seller's affidavit of title, and the surveyor's cover letter. Each has been read in full, every stated total and date interval has been "
     "recomputed, and each document has been tested against the other four.")

para("The record-title burden on the fee parcels is, in most respects, ordinary for a Texas wind project: utility, pipeline, road, drainage and "
     "water-line easements, tract mineral severances, and standard printed exceptions. Individually, none of those defeats the project. The risk in "
     "this transaction lies elsewhere — in five clusters:")

numitem("**Seller-level liabilities that reach the asset being sold.** A UCC-1 and deed of trust ($9.83 million payoff), an IRS federal tax lien "
        "($523,180), an abstract of judgment ($387,450), a mechanic's lien ($214,800) and delinquent 2024 ad valorem taxes ($1,246,088 before "
        "penalties). The judgment and the federal tax lien are against the Seller, not the Project Company, and therefore do not attach to the "
        "land (Commitment, Items 29 and 32) — but the asset being purchased is the membership interest that those liens can reach. See Sections 5.1 and 10.","(i)")
numitem("**Four priority and land-use problems that constrain siting or tenure.** A perpetual conservation easement prohibiting structures over "
        "15 feet on Parcel 44 (Item 51); a perpetual covenant prohibiting structures over 35 feet on Parcels 22 and 23 (Item 14); a covenant "
        "restricting Parcels 45 and 46 to residential and agricultural uses until November 2, 2040 (Item 52); and a senior deed of trust on "
        "Parcels 33–39 ($2,415,000 outstanding) recorded before the surface lease, with no SNDA obtained (Items 24 and 53; B-I Item 8).","(ii)")
numitem("**A live challenge to 640 acres of the leasehold.** The lis pendens recorded March 5, 2025 in Cause No. 2025-CI-03221 alleges that the "
        "Parcel 20 lease was executed without authority and that a community property agreement was forged. The affected Sturbridge parcels "
        "(20–23) are also the parcels that cannot be reconciled on acreage and that have no Schedule B-II lease-memorandum item. See Sections 5.2, 5.3 and 4.4.","(iii)")
numitem("**Acreage that no document reconciles.** One stated total is 8,412 acres; another is 8,832 acres; the underlying schedules sum to "
        "9,232, 9,234 and 9,252 acres respectively. Each of four documents states \"5,052\" leased acres, yet none of their own line items sums to "
        "5,052. See Section 4 — this is the most significant analytical finding in the report.","(iv)")
numitem("**A seller affidavit that is contradicted by the other documents at nine specific points.** It also refers to a survey prepared by a "
        "different firm bearing a different date, misstates the deed types and acquisition period, omits every monetary lien and the lis pendens "
        "from what it calls a complete accounting, and is not properly acknowledged. See Section 7.","(v)")

para("Two further structural points belong at the front of any report to Buyer. First, the commitment proposes to insure **Ridgeline Power "

     "assignment of membership interests — which cannot convey real property. Second, the commitment is **unexecuted** in the copy produced, and "
     "under its own terms is not binding until countersigned. See Section 3.")

h3("5.1.1  Item 6 — Delinquent Bexar County taxes (highest-priority lien)")
para("The 2024 Bexar County assessment is $1,284,560.00 against Parcels 1–31; $38,472.00 has been paid, leaving **$1,246,088.00** delinquent since "
     "February 1, 2025 (Item 6; the arithmetic reproduces exactly [verified]). The property is classified under agricultural (1-d-1) open-space "
     "valuation under Texas Tax Code §23.54, which is itself an issue (Section 5.7.5). Schedule B-I Item 3(a) requires payment in full including "
     "penalties and interest.")
para("Two points deserve emphasis. First, a Texas ad valorem tax lien is not merely another encumbrance: it attaches to the property on January 1 of "
     "the tax year and, under Texas Tax Code §§32.01 and 32.05, has priority over every other lien, including the deed of trust and any mechanic's "
     "lien. Nothing else in this package outranks it. Second, it is accruing. Under Texas Tax Code §33.01 a 6% penalty attaches on February 1 rising "
     "to 12% on July 1, and interest runs at 1% per month. On the unpaid balance that is approximately **$112,148 by April 1, 2025, $224,296 by July 1, "
     "2025, and $249,218 by October 1, 2025** [verified] — that is, roughly **$83,000 a month** once the penalty steps up. These are statutory "
     "computations for planning purposes; the tax office's collection figure at closing governs.")
para("The affidavit represents that all taxes through 2024 \"have been paid in full or are not yet due and payable\" and that \"no penalties, interest, "
     "or collection fees have accrued\" (Affidavit §5.1). That statement is directly contradicted by Item 6 and by B-I Item 3(a), which recites the same "
     "$1,246,088 delinquency. This is the clearest of the affidavit's misstatements and is dealt with at AF-1 in Section 7.")

h3("5.1.2  Items 8 and 9 — Great Plains National Bank deed of trust and UCC-1")
para("The deed of trust secures a $12,750,000 note, encumbers all 19 fee parcels, and stands at approximately $9,834,200 plus per diem interest "
     "(Items 8 and B-I Item 4(a)). The UCC-1 secures the same debt and covers \"all personal property and fixtures now owned or hereafter acquired and "
     "located on or related to the Windfield Creek Wind Farm project, including accounts, chattel paper, equipment, general intangibles, and proceeds\" "
     "(Item 9). A UCC-3 termination must be filed with the Texas Secretary of State; a release of the deed of trust must be recorded in Bexar County "
     "(B-I Item 4(a)–(b)).")
para("One description conflicts, and it matters for collateral. The commitment describes Item 8 as a \"Deed of Trust\". The affidavit describes the "
     "same instrument as a **\"Deed of Trust, Assignment of Leases and Rents, Security Agreement, and Fixture Filing\"** (Affidavit §3.4(a)). A fixture "
     "filing recorded in the real property records encumbers fixtures as against real property claimants, and an assignment of leases and rents reaches "
     "the rents of the encumbered property. If the affidavit's fuller description is right — and the safer assumption is that it is — then the "
     "commitment's Item 8 exception **understates the collateral**, and the release obtained at closing must be drafted to release the fixture filing "
     "and to reassign the leases and rents, not merely to reconvey the deed of trust. Ask the title officer to confirm the full title of the recorded "
     "instrument (Section 12, request 4).")
para("A second, purely practical point: the lender being paid off and the lender proposed to fund the construction/term loan are the **same bank** "
     "(Items 8–9; Sched. A ¶2(b)). See Section 3.4 on the resulting sequencing and the August 15, 2025 payoff expiry.")

h3("5.1.3  Item 31 — GeoTech Drilling mechanic's lien ($214,800)")
para("GeoTech Drilling Services LLC filed a mechanic's lien affidavit on February 10, 2025 in Volume 19001, Page 0450, Bexar County, in the amount of "
     "$214,800.00 for geotechnical testing and boring services performed on Parcels 1–10 between October 2024 and January 2025 (Item 31). Schedule B-I "
     "Item 4(c) requires a full release, or alternatively that the insured bond around the lien under Texas Property Code Chapter 53.")
para("The lien is corroborated rather than merely asserted: the surveyor observed **approximately fourteen capped geotechnical test boring locations** on "
     "Parcels 1–10 during fieldwork, consistent with the investigation the lien describes (Survey §6, Item 31). The work claimed is therefore physically "
     "evidenced on the site, which materially weakens any argument that the lien is spurious.")
para("On priority, a Texas mechanic's lien is inchoate from the commencement of construction and relates back to that date under Texas Property Code "
     "§53.124; the work here began in October 2024, well after the 2022 deed of trust, so the bank's mortgage should be senior to the mechanic's lien "
     "[legal characterisation — confirm with counsel]. That protects the lender, not Buyer: the lien still encumbers the fee parcels on which the "
     "project's first ten parcels and much of the initial civil works sit, and it must be cleared before the title company will insure, regardless of "
     "where it sits in the priority queue.")
para("The affidavit is flatly contrary. It represents that \"there are no mechanic's liens, materialmen's liens, constitutional liens, or claims for "
     "unpaid labor, services, or materials affecting the Property\", that \"no lien claimant has given the Project Company notice of a claim or filed an "
     "affidavit claiming a lien under Texas Property Code Chapter 53\", and that all contractors \"have been paid in full\" and that \"no amounts are "
     "currently outstanding or in dispute\" (Affidavit §§6.2–6.3). Each of those statements is untrue on the face of Item 31, and the affidavit was "
     "sworn after the lien was filed and recorded.")

h3("5.1.4  Item 29 — Steelform Construction abstract of judgment ($387,450)")
para("A judgment for $387,450.00 plus 5.0% post-judgment interest from November 15, 2024 was rendered in Cause No. 2024-CI-18842, 407th Judicial "
     "District Court, Bexar County, in favour of Steelform Construction Inc. against **Lone Prairie Renewables Inc.** — the Seller, not the Project "
     "Company. The abstract of judgment was filed January 22, 2025 (Item 29). Interest to April 1, 2025 is approximately $7,271, giving $394,721; to "
     "January 1, 2026, $21,867, giving $409,317 [verified].")
para("The commitment's note is correct: because the judgment debtor is not the record owner of any project parcel, the abstract creates a lien on the "
     "Seller's Bexar County real property, of which there is none, and the Company properly requires disposition under B-I Item 4(e). But the "
     "transaction risk is not extinguished by that analysis. Buyer is purchasing **the Seller's membership interest** — personal property of the "
     "judgment debtor — and a judgment creditor may reach it by execution or charging order. The lien should be satisfied and the abstract released at "
     "closing out of Seller's proceeds, or the proceeds attributable to the interest escrowed pending release [legal characterisation — confirm with "
     "counsel]. The affidavit's statement that \"no abstract of judgment has been filed against the Project Company\" (Affidavit §6.5) is literally "
     "correct because the debtor is the parent, but it is materially misleading in a document delivered to support a purchase of the parent's equity; "
     "and the further statement that \"neither the Seller nor the Project Company is a party to any litigation ... that could result in the imposition "
     "of a lien\" (Affidavit §7.4) is simply false, since the Seller is the defendant.")

h3("5.1.5  Item 32 — Federal tax lien ($523,180)")
para("The IRS filed a notice of federal tax lien on December 18, 2024 (File No. FTL-2024-00891) against Lone Prairie Renewables Inc. for the 2022 third "
     "and fourth quarters: $412,600 unpaid employment tax, $67,340 penalty and $43,240 interest, totalling $523,180 (arithmetic reproduces [verified]). "
     "Schedule B-I Item 4(d) requires either a Certificate of Release or a Certificate of Subordination or Discharge under 26 U.S.C. §6325.")
para("The commitment notes both the position and the reason it matters: the lien \"attaches to all property and rights to property of the taxpayer, "
     "which may include the taxpayer's membership interest in Windfield Creek Energy LLC\" (Item 32). That is the correct analysis. Under IRC §6321 the "
     "lien attaches to all property and rights to property of the taxpayer, and a membership interest is such property. Under §6323 a purchaser is "
     "protected against an unfiled lien, but this lien **is** filed. The practical consequence is that a discharge under §6325(b) as to the membership "
     "interest, or payment of the $523,180, is required before Buyer can take the equity free of it — a point the title commitment, focused as it is on "
     "the land, does not make. Engage tax counsel on the §6325 mechanics and on whether the transaction as structured is a bulk sale requiring "
     "notification under IRC §6903 [legal characterisation].")
para("The affidavit states that \"no federal, state, or local tax lien has been filed against the Project Company\", that the Company \"is current on all "
     "federal, state, and local tax obligations\" and that \"no taxing authority has asserted a claim for unpaid taxes against the Project Company\" "
     "(Affidavit §6.4). Those sentences are carefully scoped to the Project Company; the lien is against the parent. The scoping does not rescue the "
     "affidavit, because §10.2 then presents its list of encumbrances as \"a complete accounting\" and omits this lien, the abstract of judgment, the "
     "mechanic's lien, the delinquent taxes and the lis pendens. See Section 7.3.")

h3("5.1.6  Item 53 — Senior lessor deed of trust on Parcels 33–39 ($2,415,000)")
para("Comal Ranch LLC granted a deed of trust on Parcels 33–39 to First Southern Title Company, as trustee, for Lone Star Savings Bank on March 1, 2020, "
     "securing a $3,200,000 note recorded in Volume 4519, Page 0201, Comal County. The surface lease was recorded later, on June 1, 2020 (Volume 4521, "
     "Page 0312). The outstanding balance is approximately $2,415,000 according to Comal Ranch's own representation in March 2025 (Item 53).")
para("This is the single largest unaddressed structural risk in the lease portfolio. First-in-time recording means the deed of trust is **senior to the "
     "surface lease**; a foreclosure by Lone Star Savings Bank would extinguish the leasehold on **1,260 acres across seven parcels** — the largest "
     "single lessor grouping in the project. Schedule B-I Item 8 correctly requires a recorded, recordable SNDA. It has not been obtained. The lease "
     "schedule records the status precisely: \"SNDA not yet requested\" (Lease Schedule N-003), and adds that the balance is supported only by an oral "
     "representation with no written estoppel. The affidavit, by contrast, states that to the best of the affiant's knowledge no lessor's fee interest "
     "is subject to any encumbrance with priority over the leasehold \"except as may be disclosed in Schedule B\" and that \"I believe that the Project "
     "Company's leasehold interest is adequately protected ... by subordination, non-disturbance, and attornment agreements obtained by the Project "
     "Company\" (Affidavit §4.5). No such agreement exists. The belief is contradicted by B-I Item 8 and by N-003. See AF-11.")
para("Two cure routes exist: obtain and record the SNDA (preferred — the lessor's lender is likely to co-operate while the loan is current), or pay off "
     "the $2,415,000 at closing and take a release. The second converts a third-party problem into a price problem and should be modelled accordingly. "
     "A third route — Buyer's lender accepting the risk — is not realistic for a leasehold position of this size.")

h3("5.1.7  Item 54 — Bexar County road improvement assessment ($48,700)")
para("Assessment No. BX-2024-RA-0445 affects Parcels 1 and 2 in the amounts of $28,200.00 and $20,500.00, totalling $48,700.00, due December 31, 2025 "
     "and not delinquent as at the effective date (Item 54; arithmetic reproduces [verified]). It is a statutory assessment lien but carries no present "
     "default exposure. The surveyor observed FM 1560 widening construction activity adjacent to the eastern boundaries of Parcels 1 and 2 during "
     "fieldwork in January and February 2025, which corroborates that the assessment relates to real, in-progress work (Survey §6, Item 54) — relevant "
     "because further assessments for the same project could follow. Schedule B-I Item 3(c) contemplates payment or a proration agreement; the affidavit "
     "acknowledges the assessment and its non-delinquent status accurately (Affidavit §5.5). **Treat as a proration item, not a title defect**, and "
     "confirm with Bexar County whether additional assessments are contemplated for the balance of the frontage.")

h3("5.1.8  Item 60 — TCEQ Notice of Violation (unquantified, open-ended)")
para("TCEQ Notice of Violation No. 2024-0892, dated October 30, 2024, alleges unauthorised discharge of stormwater from construction activities on "
     "Parcel 6 in violation of the Texas Water Code, and references a potential administrative penalty of **up to $25,000 per day of violation**. No "
     "consent order, agreed order or resolution has been filed of record (Item 60). The surveyor's independent field observation is consistent with the "
     "notice: \"evidence of prior earth disturbance and sediment tracking ... including an area of exposed subsoil and silt deposits along a drainage "
     "path\" in the vicinity of turbine T-15 on Parcel 6 (Survey §6, Item 60).")
para("For title purposes the Company excepts any lien arising from the notice. For transaction purposes the exposure is unquantified and potentially "
     "open-ended, and it cannot be insured against. The affidavit represents that the Company \"has not received any notice of violation ... from any "
     "federal, state, or local environmental agency, including ... the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality\" and that \"no administrative penalty, "
     "compliance order, or consent decree has been issued, proposed, or is pending\" (Affidavit §8.2), and separately that the Company \"has obtained all "
     "environmental permits, approvals, and authorizations necessary ... including all applicable stormwater permits\" (Affidavit §8.4). Both statements "
     "are contradicted by Item 60 and by the survey finding. See AF-9.")

h2("5.2  Title and litigation matters")

h3("5.2.1  Item 30 — Lis pendens on Parcel 20 and the Parcels 20–23 leasehold")
para("A Notice of Lis Pendens was filed March 5, 2025 in Volume 19010, Page 0012, Bexar County, in Cause No. 2025-CI-03221, 150th Judicial District "
     "Court. The plaintiff is **Ronald Sturbridge, individually and as heir of Harold Sturbridge**, who died June 3, 2024; the defendant is Windfield "
     "Creek Energy LLC. The petition alleges that the Parcel 20 surface lease was executed by Harold Sturbridge **without authority**, and that the "
     "Community Property Agreement between Harold and Mabel Sturbridge purportedly authorising Harold to act for both spouses was **forged**. The relief "
     "sought is to void the lease, quiet title in the Sturbridge heirs, and recover damages (Item 30).")
para("Three features make this more serious than a routine boundary suit:")
bullet("**It attacks the instrument, not the record.** A lis pendens gives constructive notice and, if the plaintiff prevails, the lease may be void ab initio — there is no question of Buyer being a protected purchaser.")
bullet("**It affects four parcels, not one.** The commitment describes the lis pendens as affecting Parcel 20 (approximately 220 acres), but Schedule B-II Item 59 states that the surface lease affecting **Parcels 20 through 23** — all leased from Harold Sturbridge — is the subject of the same dispute, and the lease schedule treats Parcels 21–23 as part of the same instrument grouping (Item 59; Lease Schedule SL-001, SL-002). If the community property agreement was forged, it was forged for all four leases, not one. **The exposure is 560 to 640 acres, not 220.**")
bullet("**The lessor is deceased and the succession is unevidenced.** The only succession document is an Affidavit of Heirship filed August 12, 2024 identifying three children as sole heirs (Item 59). No probate is evidenced; the affidavit of heirship addresses neither Mabel Sturbridge's interest (the very interest said to have been forged into the community property agreement) nor the possibility of other claimants. The title company records the heirs as Ronald Sturbridge, Karen Sturbridge-Wells and Matthew Sturbridge.")
bullet("**There is a gap in acreage that tracks the same parcels.** Parcel 20's acreage is stated inconsistently within the commitment (198 v. 220 acres — Section 4.3) and Parcels 20–23 are the only lease group whose acreage cannot be reconciled and the only group with **no Schedule B-II lease-memorandum item**. See Section 4.4.")
para("Schedule B-I Item 7 offers three resolutions: a final non-appealable judgment dismissing the action with prejudice and cancelling the lis pendens; "
     "a recorded settlement or release; or agreement by the Proposed Insured to accept the exception in Item 30 without deletion. The third is not a "
     "cure; it is an agreement to own a 220–640 acre leasehold with no insurance and a live title challenge, and it should be priced as such. "
     "**Recommendation:** obtain a litigation opinion from Seller's counsel on the merits and the forgery allegation, a reserve or escrow in an amount "
     "at least equal to the capitalised value of the four parcels' rent and development value, a specific indemnity from Seller that survives closing, "
     "and an alternative layout that does not depend on Parcels 20–23 if the matter is unresolved at closing. If the parcel grouping cannot be "
     "delivered clean, this is a candidate for a price adjustment rather than a holdback.")

h3("5.2.2  Item 59 — Affidavit of Heirship; succession and capacity")
para("Beyond the lis pendens, the death of Harold Sturbridge on June 3, 2024 raises a straightforward conveyancing question that no document in the "
     "package answers: **whether the Sturbridge leases survive the lessor's death and whether the present lessor of record has capacity to perform.** "
     "A lease is a contract and ordinarily survives the death of a party; but if Harold lacked authority at the outset (the lis pendens allegation), "
     "succession does not cure it, and if Mabel's community interest was never validly committed, the heirs take subject to that interest. The Affidavit "
     "of Heirship identifies three children and is silent on Mabel. Texas heirship determinations require more than an ex parte affidavit where the "
     "succession is contested — which, here, it is [legal characterisation].")
para("**Recommendation:** obtain (i) the full probate or heirship record, (ii) a ratification and estoppel certificate from all three heirs confirming "
     "the leases, their terms, rent status and no defaults, or (iii) if the heirs will not ratify, treat the parcels as unavailable. Do not accept the "
     "Affidavit of Heirship as sufficient evidence of authority to lease.")
