h3("5.3.1  Term sufficiency — the Hoffman lease (Item 22)")
para("Eight of the nine leases run 30 years from 2020 with two 10-year renewals, giving a maximum term to 2070 and an initial expiry in 2050. The "
     "**Hoffman Family Trust lease (Parcels 28–30, 520 acres) runs 25 years with no renewal options**, expiring **April 2, 2045** (Item 22; Lease "
     "Schedule N-002). The commitment itself flags the point (\"The Company notes that this lease has a shorter term and no renewal options compared to "
     "the other surface leases on the Project Site\").")
para("Measured against the project: the lease schedule records an anticipated commercial operation date in late 2026 or early 2027 and a 25–30 year "
     "turbine life (Lease Schedule N-002). A 25-year operating life from 2027 runs to 2052; a 30-year life to 2057. The Hoffman lease expires in "
     "**2045 — 7 years short of a 25-year operating life and 12 years short of 30** [verified]. Even the 30-year leases at 2050 fall short of a "
     "2052–2057 operating horizon unless the first renewal is exercised, which makes the renewal mechanics commercially important, not academic.")
para("Three consequences follow. First, **the affidavit's representation is overstated**: \"the term of each surface lease, together with all available "
     "renewal and extension options ... is sufficient for the anticipated useful life of the wind energy generation facilities\" (Affidavit §4.6) "
     "cannot be true of a lease that expires in 2045 with no extension mechanism at all. Second, lenders commonly require land control for the debt "
     "tenor plus a tail; 520 acres without renewal will be an exception in the credit agreement unless amended. Third, the surveyor's siting analysis "
     "does not consider tenure at all, and two of the three Hoffman parcels carry Bandera Electric easements (Item 18), further reducing developable "
     "area on the shortest-tenure land in the project.")
para("**Recommendation:** negotiate an amendment adding two 10-year options (or a term extension) **before** closing, as a condition. Seller's "
     "co-operation should be a PSA obligation. If the trust will not amend, either price the 520 acres as a 2045 asset with decommissioning "
     "obligations brought forward, or exclude the parcels from the collateral package [inference].")

h3("5.3.2  Missing Schedule B-II lease items for Parcels 20–23")
para("Schedule B-II contains lease-memorandum items for Parcels 24 through 47 (Items 20–26) but **none for Parcels 20, 21, 22 or 23**, notwithstanding "
     "that the memoranda for those parcels are cited by recording reference in the Schedule A descriptions (Vol. 17680, Pg. 0310; Vol. 17680, Pg. 0387; "
     "Vol. 17695, Pg. 0101; Vol. 17695, Pg. 0178). The inconsistency is not merely presentational: the seven scheduled items are the exceptions against "
     "which the leasehold estate (and the lender's leasehold mortgage position) is delineated, and the four unscheduled parcels are the four parcels "
     "carrying the lis pendens and the succession problem. Whatever the cause, **640 acres of the leasehold have no scheduled exception item** — the "
     "opposite of the usual concern, and one that should be corrected in the amended commitment (Section 12, request 2). It also feeds the 5,052-acre "
     "reconstruction in Section 4.4.")

h3("5.3.3  Parcel 32 — cross-county recording dispute")
para("The Sanchez lease covers Parcel 31 (Bexar County) and Parcel 32 (Comal County). The commitment states that the memorandum recorded in Volume 17801, "
     "Page 0055, Bexar County is \"cross-filed in Volume 4502, Page 0078, Official Public Records, Comal County\" and Exhibit A records that Comal "
     "reference for Parcel 32 (Item 23; Sched. A ¶4, Parcel 32; Exh. A). The lease schedule states the opposite: that the memorandum \"was recorded only "
     "in Bexar County\" with \"no Comal County recording found\", flags a constructive-notice gap and recommends recording (Lease Schedule N-005; "
     "Encumbrances on Lessor Parcels, SL-006).")
para("One of the two is wrong and the difference is real: if there is no Comal County record, the leasehold in Parcel 32 may be vulnerable to "
     "encumbrances recorded in Comal County after May 2020 without actual notice. **Resolve by obtaining a certified copy of the Comal County record "
     "at Volume 4502, Page 0078** (Section 12, request 6). If it does not exist, record immediately and run a Comal County search from May 2020.")

h3("5.3.4  Estoppels and the leases themselves")
para("No lessor estoppel certificate exists for any of the nine leases (Lease Schedule N-003 records none for Comal Ranch; N-009 recommends obtaining "
     "them). Only memoranda of lease are of record; the lease instruments themselves were not provided. That means the affidavit's broad representations "
     "— that each lease grants the right to construct, operate, maintain, repair, replace and decommission turbines, met towers, collection systems, "

h3("5.1.1  Item 6 — Delinquent Bexar County taxes (highest-priority lien)")
para("The 2024 Bexar County assessment is $1,284,560.00 against Parcels 1–31; $38,472.00 has been paid, leaving **$1,246,088.00** delinquent since "
     "February 1, 2025 (Item 6; the arithmetic reproduces exactly [verified]). The property is classified under agricultural (1-d-1) open-space "
     "valuation under Texas Tax Code §23.54, which is itself an issue (Section 5.7.5). Schedule B-I Item 3(a) requires payment in full including "
     "penalties and interest.")
para("Two points deserve emphasis. First, a Texas ad valorem tax lien is not merely another encumbrance: it attaches to the property on January 1 of "
     "the tax year and, under Texas Tax Code §§32.01 and 32.05, has priority over every other lien, including the deed of trust and any mechanic's "
     "lien. Nothing else in this package outranks it. Second, it is accruing. Under Texas Tax Code §33.01 a 6% penalty attaches on February 1 rising "
     "to 12% on July 1, and interest runs at 1% per month. On the unpaid balance that is approximately **$112,148 by April 1, 2025, $224,296 by July 1, "
     "2025, and $249,218 by October 1, 2025** [verified] — that is, roughly **$83,000 a month** once the penalty steps up. These are statutory "
     "computations for planning purposes; the tax office's collection figure at closing governs.")
para("The affidavit represents that all taxes through 2024 \"have been paid in full or are not yet due and payable\" and that \"no penalties, interest, "
     "or collection fees have accrued\" (Affidavit §5.1). That statement is directly contradicted by Item 6 and by B-I Item 3(a), which recites the same "
     "$1,246,088 delinquency. This is the clearest of the affidavit's misstatements and is dealt with at AF-1 in Section 7.")

h3("5.1.2  Items 8 and 9 — Great Plains National Bank deed of trust and UCC-1")
para("The deed of trust secures a $12,750,000 note, encumbers all 19 fee parcels, and stands at approximately $9,834,200 plus per diem interest "
     "(Items 8 and B-I Item 4(a)). The UCC-1 secures the same debt and covers \"all personal property and fixtures now owned or hereafter acquired and "
     "located on or related to the Windfield Creek Wind Farm project, including accounts, chattel paper, equipment, general intangibles, and proceeds\" "
     "(Item 9). A UCC-3 termination must be filed with the Texas Secretary of State; a release of the deed of trust must be recorded in Bexar County "
     "(B-I Item 4(a)–(b)).")
para("One description conflicts, and it matters for collateral. The commitment describes Item 8 as a \"Deed of Trust\". The affidavit describes the "
     "same instrument as a **\"Deed of Trust, Assignment of Leases and Rents, Security Agreement, and Fixture Filing\"** (Affidavit §3.4(a)). A fixture "
     "filing recorded in the real property records encumbers fixtures as against real property claimants, and an assignment of leases and rents reaches "
     "the rents of the encumbered property. If the affidavit's fuller description is right — and the safer assumption is that it is — then the "
     "commitment's Item 8 exception **understates the collateral**, and the release obtained at closing must be drafted to release the fixture filing "
     "and to reassign the leases and rents, not merely to reconvey the deed of trust. Ask the title officer to confirm the full title of the recorded "
     "instrument (Section 12, request 4).")
para("A second, purely practical point: the lender being paid off and the lender proposed to fund the construction/term loan are the **same bank** "

para("The lien is corroborated rather than merely asserted: the surveyor observed **approximately fourteen capped geotechnical test boring locations** on "

     "evidenced on the site, which materially weakens any argument that the lien is spurious.")
para("On priority, a Texas mechanic's lien is inchoate from the commencement of construction and relates back to that date under Texas Property Code "
     "§53.124; the work here began in October 2024, well after the 2022 deed of trust, so the bank's mortgage should be senior to the mechanic's lien "
     "[legal characterisation — confirm with counsel]. That protects the lender, not Buyer: the lien still encumbers the fee parcels on which the "
     "project's first ten parcels and much of the initial civil works sit, and it must be cleared before the title company will insure, regardless of "

h2("5.2  Title and litigation matters")

h3("5.2.1  Item 30 — Lis pendens on Parcel 20 and the Parcels 20–23 leasehold")
para("A Notice of Lis Pendens was filed March 5, 2025 in Volume 19010, Page 0012, Bexar County, in Cause No. 2025-CI-03221, 150th Judicial District "
     "Court. The plaintiff is **Ronald Sturbridge, individually and as heir of Harold Sturbridge**, who died June 3, 2024; the defendant is Windfield "
     "Creek Energy LLC. The petition alleges that the Parcel 20 surface lease was executed by Harold Sturbridge **without authority**, and that the "
     "Community Property Agreement between Harold and Mabel Sturbridge purportedly authorising Harold to act for both spouses was **forged**. The relief "
     "sought is to void the lease, quiet title in the Sturbridge heirs, and recover damages (Item 30).")
para("Three features make this more serious than a routine boundary suit:")
bullet("**It attacks the instrument, not the record.** A lis pendens gives constructive notice and, if the plaintiff prevails, the lease may be void ab initio — there is no question of Buyer being a protected purchaser.")
bullet("**It affects four parcels, not one.** The commitment describes the lis pendens as affecting Parcel 20 (approximately 220 acres), but Schedule B-II Item 59 states that the surface lease affecting **Parcels 20 through 23** — all leased from Harold Sturbridge — is the subject of the same dispute, and the lease schedule treats Parcels 21–23 as part of the same instrument grouping (Item 59; Lease Schedule SL-001, SL-002). If the community property agreement was forged, it was forged for all four leases, not one. **The exposure is 560 to 640 acres, not 220.**")
bullet("**The lessor is deceased and the succession is unevidenced.** The only succession document is an Affidavit of Heirship filed August 12, 2024 identifying three children as sole heirs (Item 59). No probate is evidenced; the affidavit of heirship addresses neither Mabel Sturbridge's interest (the very interest said to have been forged into the community property agreement) nor the possibility of other claimants. The title company records the heirs as Ronald Sturbridge, Karen Sturbridge-Wells and Matthew Sturbridge.")
bullet("**There is a gap in acreage that tracks the same parcels.** Parcel 20's acreage is stated inconsistently within the commitment (198 v. 220 acres — Section 4.3) and Parcels 20–23 are the only lease group whose acreage cannot be reconciled and the only group with **no Schedule B-II lease-memorandum item**. See Section 4.4.")
para("Schedule B-I Item 7 offers three resolutions: a final non-appealable judgment dismissing the action with prejudice and cancelling the lis pendens; "
     "a recorded settlement or release; or agreement by the Proposed Insured to accept the exception in Item 30 without deletion. The third is not a "
     "cure; it is an agreement to own a 220–640 acre leasehold with no insurance and a live title challenge, and it should be priced as such. "
     "**Recommendation:** obtain a litigation opinion from Seller's counsel on the merits and the forgery allegation, a reserve or escrow in an amount "
     "at least equal to the capitalised value of the four parcels' rent and development value, a specific indemnity from Seller that survives closing, "
     "and an alternative layout that does not depend on Parcels 20–23 if the matter is unresolved at closing. If the parcel grouping cannot be "
     "delivered clean, this is a candidate for a price adjustment rather than a holdback.")

h3("5.2.2  Item 59 — Affidavit of Heirship; succession and capacity")
para("Beyond the lis pendens, the death of Harold Sturbridge on June 3, 2024 raises a straightforward conveyancing question that no document in the "
     "package answers: **whether the Sturbridge leases survive the lessor's death and whether the present lessor of record has capacity to perform.** "
     "A lease is a contract and ordinarily survives the death of a party; but if Harold lacked authority at the outset (the lis pendens allegation), "
     "succession does not cure it, and if Mabel's community interest was never validly committed, the heirs take subject to that interest. The Affidavit "
     "of Heirship identifies three children and is silent on Mabel. Texas heirship determinations require more than an ex parte affidavit where the "
     "succession is contested — which, here, it is [legal characterisation].")
para("**Recommendation:** obtain (i) the full probate or heirship record, (ii) a ratification and estoppel certificate from all three heirs confirming "
     "the leases, their terms, rent status and no defaults, or (iii) if the heirs will not ratify, treat the parcels as unavailable. Do not accept the "
     "Affidavit of Heirship as sufficient evidence of authority to lease.")

h3("5.3.1  Term sufficiency — the Hoffman lease (Item 22)")
para("Eight of the nine leases run 30 years from 2020 with two 10-year renewals, giving a maximum term to 2070 and an initial expiry in 2050. The "
     "**Hoffman Family Trust lease (Parcels 28–30, 520 acres) runs 25 years with no renewal options**, expiring **April 2, 2045** (Item 22; Lease "
     "Schedule N-002). The commitment itself flags the point (\"The Company notes that this lease has a shorter term and no renewal options compared to "
     "the other surface leases on the Project Site\").")
para("Measured against the project: the lease schedule records an anticipated commercial operation date in late 2026 or early 2027 and a 25–30 year "
     "turbine life (Lease Schedule N-002). A 25-year operating life from 2027 runs to 2052; a 30-year life to 2057. The Hoffman lease expires in "
     "**2045 — 7 years short of a 25-year operating life and 12 years short of 30** [verified]. Even the 30-year leases at 2050 fall short of a "
     "2052–2057 operating horizon unless the first renewal is exercised, which makes the renewal mechanics commercially important, not academic.")
para("Three consequences follow. First, **the affidavit's representation is overstated**: \"the term of each surface lease, together with all available "
     "renewal and extension options ... is sufficient for the anticipated useful life of the wind energy generation facilities\" (Affidavit §4.6) "
     "cannot be true of a lease that expires in 2045 with no extension mechanism at all. Second, lenders commonly require land control for the debt "
     "tenor plus a tail; 520 acres without renewal will be an exception in the credit agreement unless amended. Third, the surveyor's siting analysis "
     "does not consider tenure at all, and two of the three Hoffman parcels carry Bandera Electric easements (Item 18), further reducing developable "
     "area on the shortest-tenure land in the project.")
para("**Recommendation:** negotiate an amendment adding two 10-year options (or a term extension) **before** closing, as a condition. Seller's "
     "co-operation should be a PSA obligation. If the trust will not amend, either price the 520 acres as a 2045 asset with decommissioning "
     "obligations brought forward, or exclude the parcels from the collateral package [inference].")

h3("5.3.2  Missing Schedule B-II lease items for Parcels 20–23")
para("Schedule B-II contains lease-memorandum items for Parcels 24 through 47 (Items 20–26) but **none for Parcels 20, 21, 22 or 23**, notwithstanding "

     "which the leasehold estate (and the lender's leasehold mortgage position) is delineated, and the four unscheduled parcels are the four parcels "
     "carrying the lis pendens and the succession problem. Whatever the cause, **640 acres of the leasehold have no scheduled exception item** — the "
     "opposite of the usual concern, and one that should be corrected in the amended commitment (Section 12, request 2). It also feeds the 5,052-acre "
     "reconstruction in Section 4.4.")

h3("5.3.3  Parcel 32 — cross-county recording dispute")
para("The Sanchez lease covers Parcel 31 (Bexar County) and Parcel 32 (Comal County). The commitment states that the memorandum recorded in Volume 17801, "
     "Page 0055, Bexar County is \"cross-filed in Volume 4502, Page 0078, Official Public Records, Comal County\" and Exhibit A records that Comal "

     "in Bexar County\" with \"no Comal County recording found\", flags a constructive-notice gap and recommends recording (Lease Schedule N-005; "
     "Encumbrances on Lessor Parcels, SL-006).")
para("One of the two is wrong and the difference is real: if there is no Comal County record, the leasehold in Parcel 32 may be vulnerable to "
     "encumbrances recorded in Comal County after May 2020 without actual notice. **Resolve by obtaining a certified copy of the Comal County record "
     "at Volume 4502, Page 0078** (Section 12, request 6). If it does not exist, record immediately and run a Comal County search from May 2020.")

h3("5.3.4  Estoppels and the leases themselves")
para("No lessor estoppel certificate exists for any of the nine leases (Lease Schedule N-003 records none for Comal Ranch; N-009 recommends obtaining "
     "them). Only memoranda of lease are of record; the lease instruments themselves were not provided. That means the affidavit's broad representations "
     "— that each lease grants the right to construct, operate, maintain, repair, replace and decommission turbines, met towers, collection systems, "
     "substations, access roads, transmission lines and O&M buildings (Affidavit §4.4), and that rent is current with no defaults (Affidavit §§4.1–4.3) "
     "— are **untested against the documents that would prove them**.")
para("Obtaining estoppels is the single highest-value diligence step available to Buyer on the lease portfolio, because each estoppel does four things at "
     "once: it confirms the acreage (Section 4), the rent (Section 4.5), the term and renewal mechanics (Section 5.3.1) and the absence of defaults and "

     "whether the lease requires consent to a change of control of the lessee (an open question under Affidavit §4.4 and relevant because the transaction "

h3("5.5.1  Parcel 44 — perpetual conservation easement (Item 51)")
para("The Texas Land Conservancy holds a conservation easement over the **entirety of Parcel 44** (approximately 180 acres) recorded September 9, 2017, "
     "which permanently restricts the property to agricultural, ranching and wildlife habitat uses and **prohibits the construction of any structure "
     "exceeding 15 feet in height**. It is perpetual, runs with the land, binds \"all successors, assigns, lessees, and occupants\", and the Conservancy "
     "holds the right to enforce by injunction. No modification, amendment or termination may occur without the Conservancy's written consent and "
     "compliance with the Texas Natural Resources Code (Item 51).")
para("The surveyor records three proposed turbine locations inside the parcel — **T-65, T-66 and T-67** — and describes the conflict as \"fatal\" in "
     "terms: \"Proposed turbines at 590 feet AGL represent a fundamental conflict with the easement terms ... turbine relocation outside Parcel 44 appears "
     "necessary unless the conservation easement can be terminated or modified, which typically requires judicial action and consent of the easement "
     "holder\" (Survey §7, conflict 5). The lease schedule reaches the same view (\"likely unresolvable — exclude from development plan\", SL-009).")
para("That assessment is right, and it should be accepted rather than negotiated. A perpetual conservation easement granted to a land trust for "
     "conservation purposes is about as close to unextinguishable as a private land-use restriction gets in Texas: termination requires either the "
     "holder's consent (which would defeat the charitable purpose for which the easement was donated and would likely require notice to, or approval by, "
     "the charity's regulators) or a judicial determination that the conservation purpose has become impossible or impracticable. Neither is a closing "
     "condition; both are multi-year projects with uncertain outcomes [legal characterisation].")
para("**Recommendation:** remove T-65, T-66 and T-67 from the layout and **exclude Parcel 44 from the developable acreage** in the PSA, the credit "
     "documents and the insured value allocation. The lease remains valid and rent remains payable ($3,600 per year on 180 acres) — the lease schedule "
     "raises the sensible question whether rent should be renegotiated if no turbines can be placed, but the lease does not appear to provide for that "
     "(SL-009). Note that the height limit is 15 feet, so the prohibition is not limited to turbines: met towers, collector substation equipment, "
     "laydown yards and access road improvements may all be caught, which further limits any use of the parcel.")

h3("5.5.2  Parcels 22 and 23 — covenant with no expiry (Item 14)")
para("A restrictive covenant recorded July 8, 2003 by the Estates of Windfield Creek Property Owners Association restricts Land to \"single-family "
     "residential purposes and agricultural uses\" and prohibits \"industrial structures exceeding 35 feet in height\". It is stated to run with the land, "
     "is binding on \"all subsequent owners, lessees, and occupants\", and has **no stated expiration date and no termination provision** (Item 14).")
para("Turbines T-30 and T-31 are sited on Parcels 22 and 23 respectively (Survey §6, Item 14). At 590 feet against a 35-foot limit, the conflict is "
     "arithmetic. What makes this item harder than a stale covenant is that it has no sunset: unlike Item 52 (Parcels 45–46), time does not solve it, so "
     "the options are limited to a recorded modification or release signed by the association and by any benefited owners who retain enforcement rights, "
     "a judicial determination that enforcement is barred (waiver, abandonment, laches or changed conditions), or relocation of the two turbines.")
para("Two further points for the file. First, the covenant predates the lease by seventeen years, so it is a **senior** burden and the lessor cannot "
     "cure it unilaterally. Second, the surveyor confirms the parcels are platted lots in \"Windfield Creek Estates, Section 2\" (Lot 14 and Lot 15 "
     "respectively) with monuments agreeing to the plat (Survey §4), so there is no argument that the covenant was mis-indexed or that the parcels are "
     "outside the subdivision. **Recommendation:** approach the association early — a POA that has not enforced a 35-foot height limit against "
     "agricultural structures for twenty years may be willing to grant a limited release for designated turbine envelopes, but it will need the "
     "benefited owners' concurrence, and that takes months. Obtain the declaration, the plats and the association's governing documents first.")

h2("5.7  Regulatory, environmental and flood matters")

h3("5.7.1  Item 19 — FAA Determinations of No Hazard expire before projected operation")
para("The FAA issued Determinations of No Hazard to Air Navigation on November 12, 2024 for 78 turbine structures at a maximum height of 590 feet AGL, in "
     "Case Nos. 2024-ASW-12345-OE through 2024-ASW-12422-OE. They are \"valid for an 18-month period expiring **May 12, 2026**\" and are listed as an "
     "informational exception only, with no representation as to continued validity (Item 19; Survey §2.1). The 18-month computation reproduces exactly "
     "[verified].")
para("The lease schedule assumes commercial operation in late 2026 or early 2027 (N-002), and the affidavit asserts the determinations \"remain in full "
     "force and effect and have not been revoked, modified, or challenged\" (Affidavit §8.5). Both can be true only for a short window: a determination "
     "that expires May 12, 2026 does not authorise construction commenced after that date. FAA practice permits a petition for extension before expiry, "
     "and a new filing is required if the structures, locations or heights change — which, given the relocations this report recommends for ten turbines "
     "(Section 6.4), is likely. **Recommendation:** calendar a filing by February 2026 at the latest, and treat the determination set as needing "
     "re-issue after the layout is finalised; make it a Seller bring-down representation that no determination has lapsed. This is a schedule risk, not a "
     "title defect, and it is not treated as one by the commitment.")

h3("5.7.2  Item 28 — Habitat Conservation Plan: the permit holder conflict")
para("USFWS Incidental Take Permit No. TE-87421C dated February 28, 2024 relates to the Golden-cheeked Warbler and imposes seasonal clearing restrictions "
     "— **no vegetation clearing from March 1 through August 31** of each year — on approximately 340 acres within **Parcels 36, 37 and 38** containing "
     "identified nesting habitat. The commitment states that \"the permit is in the name of **Windfield Creek Energy LLC**\" (Item 28), and the affidavit "
     "confirms that the Project Company holds the permit and is in compliance with it (Affidavit §8.3).")
para("The lease schedule says the opposite: \"The ITP was issued to **Comal Ranch LLC** — confirm whether the ITP is assignable or whether a new ITP must be "
     "obtained by the project company\" (N-007). This is a direct conflict on a point that determines whether the project may lawfully take the species "
     "during construction at all, and it cannot be resolved by inference. Resolve by obtaining the face of the permit from USFWS (Section 12, request 9).")
para("Two consequences follow either way. First, a **six-month annual clearing blackout** on 340 acres inside the largest lease grouping is a hard "
     "scheduling constraint: clearing on Parcels 36–38 can only occur September through February, which interacts with Texas weather, with the FAA window "
     "and with the lender's construction schedule. Model it, and consider whether the affected turbines can be sequenced into a winter-only work front. "
     "Second, if the permit is in Comal Ranch LLC's name, the project company has been operating on another entity's authorisation — a compliance "
     "exposure the affidavit's §8.3 and §8.4 statements would not survive.")
para("The surveyor plotted the 340-acre overlay from the environmental consultant's shapefiles at Sheets 14–15 but expressly did not verify the habitat "
     "boundary or conduct any biological assessment (Survey §6, Item 28; §9 note 10). The boundary should be confirmed by the environmental consultant "
     "against the final layout before clearing is scheduled.")

h3("5.7.3  Item 33 — FEMA Zone AE and turbine T-42")
para("Portions of Parcels 15, 16 and 40 lie in Zone AE on FIRM Panel 48029C0740G (effective June 2, 2021): approximately 32, 18 and 37 acres "
     "respectively, totalling approximately **87 acres** — which reproduces from the components [verified] (Item 33; Survey §6, Item 33). Proposed "
     "turbine **T-42 on Parcel 40** sits approximately 120 feet inside the Zone AE boundary, at a surveyed ground elevation of approximately **1,038 feet "
     "NAVD88 against a base flood elevation of approximately 1,042 feet NAVD88 — about four feet below the BFE** (Survey §6, Item 33; Cover Letter §4). "
     "Access road AR-22 also crosses Zone AE on Parcel 15 for approximately 400 linear feet (Survey §6, Item 33).")
para("The exposure is not title risk but lender and permitting risk: a turbine pad, foundation and crane staging area inside a Special Flood Hazard Area "
     "and below BFE will engage the lender's flood covenants and NFIP lending requirements, and a floodplain development permit under 44 C.F.R. Part 60. "
     "The three routes are relocation (fastest and cheapest), a LOMA or LOMR-F (which requires demonstrating the pad is above BFE — and on the surveyor's "
     "figures it is not), or a permit with elevation certificate and flood insurance. The surveyor's and cover letter's recommendations align. "
     "**Recommendation:** relocate T-42; it is a single turbine and the floodplain is only one parcel.")

h3("5.7.4  Item 60 — TCEQ enforcement")
para("Dealt with at Section 5.1.8. In brief: an open Notice of Violation with a penalty exposure of up to $25,000 per day, no consent order of record, "
     "corroborated by the surveyor's field observation of sediment tracking near turbine T-15 on Parcel 6, and flatly denied by affidavit §§8.2 and 8.4. "
     "The item is uninsurable and must be resolved with TCEQ or specifically indemnified.")

h3("5.7.5  Agricultural rollback exposure — not an exception, but a material omission")
para("Every source describes the property as assessed under agricultural (1-d-1) open-space valuation under Texas Tax Code §23.54 (Item 6; Item 7; "
     "Affidavit §5.3; Survey §9 note 11). The affidavit represents that the valuation \"has been continuously maintained ... since prior to the Project "
     "Company's acquisition\", that the Company \"has not taken any action that would cause a change-of-use determination\", and that no rollback taxes "
     "are due (Affidavit §§5.3–5.4). All three statements are true **as at the date of the affidavit** and all three will cease to be true on construction.")
para("When open-space land is converted to a non-qualifying use, Texas Tax Code §§23.55 and 23.76 impose a rollback: the difference between the taxes "
     "actually imposed and the taxes that would have been imposed at market value, for the statutory look-back period, **plus a penalty**. A "
     "1-d-1 designation is difficult to maintain on land carrying turbines, crane pads, substations and 62 miles of access roads, so the conversion will "
     "occur and the rollback will be assessed on the then-current roll [legal characterisation; the look-back period and penalty should be confirmed with "
     "the appraisal districts].")
para("No document in the package quantifies this. What can be said is that the current assessments are plainly open-space values, not market values: the "
     "2024 combined assessment is $1,896,900 against approximately 8,400 acres — about **$226 per acre** [verified]. If market value on conversion is a "
     "multiple of that, the rollback on 8,400 acres is a multiple of the current annual tax bill in a single year, and it recurs across the roll years. "
     "**Recommendation:** obtain written rollback estimates from the Bexar County Appraisal District and the Comal County Appraisal District for each "
     "parcel on the anticipated change-of-use date; allocate the liability expressly in the PSA (it should fall on Seller for periods before closing); "
     "and require a specific indemnity with a survival period at least equal to the rollback look-back plus a year. This is the largest unquantified "
     "number in the transaction and it is absent from the affidavit's \"complete accounting\".")

h3("5.7.1  Item 19 — FAA Determinations of No Hazard expire before projected operation")
para("The FAA issued Determinations of No Hazard to Air Navigation on November 12, 2024 for 78 turbine structures at a maximum height of 590 feet AGL, in "
     "Case Nos. 2024-ASW-12345-OE through 2024-ASW-12422-OE. They are \"valid for an 18-month period expiring **May 12, 2026**\" and are listed as an "
     "informational exception only, with no representation as to continued validity (Item 19; Survey §2.1). The 18-month computation reproduces exactly "
     "[verified].")
para("The lease schedule assumes commercial operation in late 2026 or early 2027 (N-002), and the affidavit asserts the determinations \"remain in full "
     "force and effect and have not been revoked, modified, or challenged\" (Affidavit §8.5). Both can be true only for a short window: a determination "
     "that expires May 12, 2026 does not authorise construction commenced after that date. FAA practice permits a petition for extension before expiry, "
     "and a new filing is required if the structures, locations or heights change — which, given the relocations this report recommends for ten turbines "
     "(Section 6.4), is likely. **Recommendation:** calendar a filing by February 2026 at the latest, and treat the determination set as needing "
     "re-issue after the layout is finalised; make it a Seller bring-down representation that no determination has lapsed. This is a schedule risk, not a "
     "title defect, and it is not treated as one by the commitment.")

h3("5.7.2  Item 28 — Habitat Conservation Plan: the permit holder conflict")
para("USFWS Incidental Take Permit No. TE-87421C dated February 28, 2024 relates to the Golden-cheeked Warbler and imposes seasonal clearing restrictions "
     "— **no vegetation clearing from March 1 through August 31** of each year — on approximately 340 acres within **Parcels 36, 37 and 38** containing "
     "identified nesting habitat. The commitment states that \"the permit is in the name of **Windfield Creek Energy LLC**\" (Item 28), and the affidavit "
     "confirms that the Project Company holds the permit and is in compliance with it (Affidavit §8.3).")
para("The lease schedule says the opposite: \"The ITP was issued to **Comal Ranch LLC** — confirm whether the ITP is assignable or whether a new ITP must be "
     "obtained by the project company\" (N-007). This is a direct conflict on a point that determines whether the project may lawfully take the species "
     "during construction at all, and it cannot be resolved by inference. Resolve by obtaining the face of the permit from USFWS (Section 12, request 9).")
para("Two consequences follow either way. First, a **six-month annual clearing blackout** on 340 acres inside the largest lease grouping is a hard "
     "scheduling constraint: clearing on Parcels 36–38 can only occur September through February, which interacts with Texas weather, with the FAA window "
     "and with the lender's construction schedule. Model it, and consider whether the affected turbines can be sequenced into a winter-only work front. "
     "Second, if the permit is in Comal Ranch LLC's name, the project company has been operating on another entity's authorisation — a compliance "
     "exposure the affidavit's §8.3 and §8.4 statements would not survive.")
para("The surveyor plotted the 340-acre overlay from the environmental consultant's shapefiles at Sheets 14–15 but expressly did not verify the habitat "
     "boundary or conduct any biological assessment (Survey §6, Item 28; §9 note 10). The boundary should be confirmed by the environmental consultant "
     "against the final layout before clearing is scheduled.")

     "Access road AR-22 also crosses Zone AE on Parcel 15 for approximately 400 linear feet (Survey §6, Item 33).")
para("The exposure is not title risk but lender and permitting risk: a turbine pad, foundation and crane staging area inside a Special Flood Hazard Area "

     "The three routes are relocation (fastest and cheapest), a LOMA or LOMR-F (which requires demonstrating the pad is above BFE — and on the surveyor's "

h3("5.7.4  Item 60 — TCEQ enforcement")

     "The item is uninsurable and must be resolved with TCEQ or specifically indemnified.")

h3("5.7.5  Agricultural rollback exposure — not an exception, but a material omission")
para("Every source describes the property as assessed under agricultural (1-d-1) open-space valuation under Texas Tax Code §23.54 (Item 6; Item 7; "
     "Affidavit §5.3; Survey §9 note 11). The affidavit represents that the valuation \"has been continuously maintained ... since prior to the Project "
     "Company's acquisition\", that the Company \"has not taken any action that would cause a change-of-use determination\", and that no rollback taxes "
     "are due (Affidavit §§5.3–5.4). All three statements are true **as at the date of the affidavit** and all three will cease to be true on construction.")
para("When open-space land is converted to a non-qualifying use, Texas Tax Code §§23.55 and 23.76 impose a rollback: the difference between the taxes "
     "actually imposed and the taxes that would have been imposed at market value, for the statutory look-back period, **plus a penalty**. A "
     "1-d-1 designation is difficult to maintain on land carrying turbines, crane pads, substations and 62 miles of access roads, so the conversion will "
     "occur and the rollback will be assessed on the then-current roll [legal characterisation; the look-back period and penalty should be confirmed with "
     "the appraisal districts].")
para("No document in the package quantifies this. What can be said is that the current assessments are plainly open-space values, not market values: the "
     "2024 combined assessment is $1,896,900 against approximately 8,400 acres — about **$226 per acre** [verified]. If market value on conversion is a "
     "multiple of that, the rollback on 8,400 acres is a multiple of the current annual tax bill in a single year, and it recurs across the roll years. "
     "**Recommendation:** obtain written rollback estimates from the Bexar County Appraisal District and the Comal County Appraisal District for each "
     "parcel on the anticipated change-of-use date; allocate the liability expressly in the PSA (it should fall on Seller for periods before closing); "
     "and require a specific indemnity with a survival period at least equal to the rollback look-back plus a year. This is the largest unquantified "
     "number in the transaction and it is absent from the affidavit's \"complete accounting\".")

numitem("**IRS federal tax lien (CC-4).** An application under 26 U.S.C. §6325 requires title evidence, an appraisal or valuation, and payment of the "
        "government's interest, and the Service does not expedite. Thirty to forty-five days from a complete application is the working assumption. "
        "As against an October 1, 2025 commitment expiry, an application not lodged by mid-August puts the closing date at risk. **This should be the "
        "first thing Seller does.**","1.")
numitem("**Lis pendens and heirship (CC-10, CC-11).** A contested forgery allegation does not settle on a closing timetable. If the matter is not "
        "resolved, the fallback is a price adjustment for Parcels 20–23 and an agreed exclusion of those parcels from the insured estate, which itself "
        "requires the title company to amend Schedule A and the survey to reflect a smaller site.","2.")
numitem("**Use restrictions and layout (CC-14 to CC-17).** The land conservancy and the two covenants will take months to resolve, if they can be "
        "resolved at all. The realistic path is a **revised layout** removing seven turbines, which then feeds back into the FAA filings (Item 19), the "
        "HCP clearing programme (Item 28), the floodplain analysis (Item 33) and the lender's independent engineer review. Starting the layout revision "
        "now, in parallel, is the only way to avoid discovering in September that the layout cannot be built.","3.")

para("Three chains of work are on the critical path, and two of them cannot be run at the same time as the others:")
numitem("**IRS federal tax lien (CC-4).** An application under 26 U.S.C. §6325 requires title evidence, an appraisal or valuation, and payment of the "
        "government's interest, and the Service does not expedite. Thirty to forty-five days from a complete application is the working assumption. "
        "As against an October 1, 2025 commitment expiry, an application not lodged by mid-August puts the closing date at risk. **This should be the "
        "first thing Seller does.**","1.")
numitem("**Lis pendens and heirship (CC-10, CC-11).** A contested forgery allegation does not settle on a closing timetable. If the matter is not "
        "resolved, the fallback is a price adjustment for Parcels 20–23 and an agreed exclusion of those parcels from the insured estate, which itself "
        "requires the title company to amend Schedule A and the survey to reflect a smaller site.","2.")
numitem("**Use restrictions and layout (CC-14 to CC-17).** The land conservancy and the two covenants will take months to resolve, if they can be "
        "resolved at all. The realistic path is a **revised layout** removing seven turbines, which then feeds back into the FAA filings (Item 19), the "
        "HCP clearing programme (Item 28), the floodplain analysis (Item 33) and the lender's independent engineer review. Starting the layout revision "
        "now, in parallel, is the only way to avoid discovering in September that the layout cannot be built.","3.")
para("Everything else — releases, tax payment, estoppels, entity documents, the survey bring-down — is capable of completion within a normal closing "

h2("10.5  Is $47,500,000 the right number?")
para("The Owner's Policy is committed at $47,500,000 (Sched. A ¶2(a)) — roughly $5,145 to $5,647 per acre depending on which acreage figure is used "
     "(Section 4.4). Two observations follow, and the second is more important than the first.")
para("First, the figure cannot be tested against the documents reviewed: no valuation, appraisal or allocation appears in any of the five. The insured "
     "amount may be a whole-asset value that includes the development upside, in which case the per-acre arithmetic is beside the point. It should "
     "nonetheless be confirmed against the purchase price allocation in the PSA and against the lender's loan-to-value test, because a policy that is "
     "under-insured at the parcel level creates a gap precisely where an encumbrance claim would bite [inference].")
para("Second, and more practically, **the monetary encumbrances against the seller-level estate total $12.37 million as at April 1, 2025 and $12.59 "
     "million as at October 1, 2025** — 26% of the policy amount — before any allowance for rollback taxes, the TCEQ penalty, the possible $2.415 million "
     "Comal Ranch payoff and the unquantifiable cost of relocating ten turbines. A policy amount that nets out to roughly three-quarters of its face value "
     "once the mandatory payoffs are accounted for should be revisited with the lender and with the title company before the Loan Policy amount is fixed. "
     "The Loan Policy amount is, in any event, still \"to be determined\" (Sched. A ¶2(b)).")

h2("10.5  Is $47,500,000 the right number?")
para("The Owner's Policy is committed at $47,500,000 (Sched. A ¶2(a)) — roughly $5,145 to $5,647 per acre depending on which acreage figure is used "
     "(Section 4.4). Two observations follow, and the second is more important than the first.")
para("First, the figure cannot be tested against the documents reviewed: no valuation, appraisal or allocation appears in any of the five. The insured "
     "amount may be a whole-asset value that includes the development upside, in which case the per-acre arithmetic is beside the point. It should "
     "nonetheless be confirmed against the purchase price allocation in the PSA and against the lender's loan-to-value test, because a policy that is "
     "under-insured at the parcel level creates a gap precisely where an encumbrance claim would bite [inference].")
para("Second, and more practically, **the monetary encumbrances against the seller-level estate total $12.37 million as at April 1, 2025 and $12.59 "
     "million as at October 1, 2025** — 26% of the policy amount — before any allowance for rollback taxes, the TCEQ penalty, the possible $2.415 million "
     "Comal Ranch payoff and the unquantifiable cost of relocating ten turbines. A policy amount that nets out to roughly three-quarters of its face value "
     "once the mandatory payoffs are accounted for should be revisited with the lender and with the title company before the Loan Policy amount is fixed. "
     "The Loan Policy amount is, in any event, still \"to be determined\" (Sched. A ¶2(b)).")

h2("11.3  Deal protections")
para("Conditions precedent protect Buyer's right to walk away; they do not compensate for what has already been misdescribed. Four protections should sit "
     "alongside them:")
bullet("**A closing escrow of $12,592,209** (the October 1, 2025 figure at Section 10.1) held until each monetary release is recorded, released against recorded instruments rather than against undertakings. If the parties prefer a smaller holdback, the release of each item should release a corresponding tranche.")
bullet("**A special indemnity** from Seller, backed by a guarantee from an entity with assets, for (i) the accuracy of the affidavit, (ii) rollback taxes, (iii) the TCEQ penalty, and (iv) any claim arising from the Sturbridge leases — with survival of not less than 24 months and, for rollback and environmental matters, the statutory limitation period plus one year.")
bullet("**Price architecture that is acreage- and turbine-sensitive.** A fixed price for a site whose acreage is uncertain by 840 acres and whose turbine count is uncertain by ten is not a fixed price. Build in an adjustment per acre for the reconciliation outcome and a schedule of reductions for each turbine that cannot be built.")
bullet("**A bring-down certificate.** It is a condition of almost every title policy that the representations on which exceptions were deleted remain true at closing. Given that the affidavit is already untrue, a closing-date certificate — and a right to re-underwrite if the bring-down is qualified — is essential.")

import re

ENCUMBRANCE SUMMARY REPORT | WINDFIELD CREEK WIND FARM                  PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL




1 Executive Summary

1.1 Purpose and principal conclusions
This report summarises and tests the encumbrance package for the acquisition by
Ridgeline Power Holdings LLC (the “Buyer”) of 100% of the membership interests in
Windfield Creek Energy LLC (the “Project Company”) from Lone Prairie Renewables
Inc. (the “Seller”). It is based on five documents: a 63-item preliminary title
commitment, an ALTA/NSPS survey narrative with certification, a nine-lease surface
lease schedule, a seller's affidavit of title, and the surveyor's cover letter. Each has
been read in full, every stated total and date interval has been recomputed, and each
document has been tested against the other four.
The record-title burden on the fee parcels is, in most respects, ordinary for a Texas
wind project: utility, pipeline, road, drainage and water-line easements, tract mineral
severances, and standard printed exceptions. Individually, none of those defeats the
project. The risk in this transaction lies elsewhere — in five clusters:
(i) Seller-level liabilities that reach the asset being sold. A UCC-1 and deed of
    trust ($9.83 million payoff), an IRS federal tax lien ($523,180), an abstract of
    judgment ($387,450), a mechanic's lien ($214,800) and delinquent 2024 ad
    valorem taxes ($1,246,088 before penalties). The judgment and the federal tax lien
    are against the Seller, not the Project Company, and therefore do not attach to the
    land (Commitment, Items 29 and 32) — but the asset being purchased is the
    membership interest that those liens can reach. See Sections 5.1 and 10.
(ii) Four priority and land-use problems that constrain siting or tenure. A
     perpetual conservation easement prohibiting structures over 15 feet on Parcel 44
     (Item 51); a perpetual covenant prohibiting structures over 35 feet on Parcels 22
     and 23 (Item 14); a covenant restricting Parcels 45 and 46 to residential and
     agricultural uses until November 2, 2040 (Item 52); and a senior deed of trust on
     Parcels 33–39 ($2,415,000 outstanding) recorded before the surface lease, with no
     SNDA obtained (Items 24 and 53; B-I Item 8).
(iii) A live challenge to 640 acres of the leasehold. The lis pendens recorded
      March 5, 2025 in Cause No. 2025-CI-03221 alleges that the Parcel 20 lease was
      executed without authority and that a community property agreement was forged.
      The affected Sturbridge parcels (20–23) are also the parcels that cannot be
      reconciled on acreage and that have no Schedule B-II lease-memorandum item.
      See Sections 5.2, 5.3 and 4.4.
(iv) Acreage that no document reconciles. One stated total is 8,412 acres; another
     is 8,832 acres; the underlying schedules sum to 9,232, 9,234 and 9,252 acres
     respectively. Each of four documents states "5,052" leased acres, yet none of their
     own line items sums to 5,052. See Section 4 — this is the most significant
     analytical finding in the report.
(v) A seller affidavit that is contradicted by the other documents at nine
    specific points. It also refers to a survey prepared by a different firm bearing a
    different date, misstates the deed types and acquisition period, omits every
    monetary lien and the lis pendens from what it calls a complete accounting, and is
    not properly acknowledged. See Section 7.


              Commitment No. BTA-2024-07831 · Windfield Creek Wind Farm · Page 3 of 75
 ENCUMBRANCE SUMMARY REPORT | WINDFIELD CREEK WIND FARM                                 PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL




Two further structural points belong at the front of any report to Buyer. First, the
commitment proposes to insure Ridgeline Power Holdings LLC as owner of estates
that remain vested in the Project Company, and Schedule B-I Item 2 proposes to create
that estate by assignment of membership interests — which cannot convey real
property. Second, the commitment is unexecuted in the copy produced, and under its
own terms is not binding until countersigned. See Section 3.

{"file_path": "response.md", "content": "# Encumbrance Summary Report — Windfield Creek Wind Farm

**Deliverable:** `encumbrance-summary-report.docx` (73 pages, 41 numbered tables, 5 appendices)

## What was reviewed

All five sources were read in full: the 63-item preliminary title commitment (BTA-2024-07831, effective 1 April 2025); the ALTA/NSPS survey narrative (TLS-2025-0294, certified 28 March 2025); the nine-lease surface lease schedule (18 April 2025); the seller's affidavit (25 April 2025); and the surveyor's cover letter.

## Method

Every stated total, subtotal, per-acre rent, per-diem, penalty and date interval in the four documents was recomputed from its underlying components; all 63 Schedule B-II items were reconciled to the surveyor's cross-reference notes, the lease schedule and the affidavit; and each document was tested against the other four. Statements are classified as extracted fact, verified computation, inference, legal characterisation or open question, and every proposition is cited to a document and section.

## Principal findings

1. **Acreage reconciles nowhere.** Two totals are stated (8,412 and 8,832 acres); the underlying schedules sum to 9,232, 9,234 and 9,252. All four documents repeat "5,052 leased acres", yet none of their line items sums to 5,052. Three of the four reconcile **exactly** to 5,052 if Parcels 21–23 (400–420 acres) are removed — the same parcels that have no Schedule B-II lease-memorandum item. The true leased acreage gap is therefore ~760–840 acres, not the 420 acres everyone repeats.
2. **Fee parcels: identical subtotals, different parcels.** 18 of 19 fee parcels carry different acreages in the commitment and the survey (up to 135 acres on Parcel 7), yet both subtotals are exactly 3,780 — offsetting errors in at least one schedule.
3. **Insuring structure mismatch.** Schedule A names Ridgeline (the buyer) as Proposed Insured for estates vested in Windfield Creek Energy LLC, and B-I Item 2 proposes to create that estate by assignment of membership interests, which cannot convey real property. The commitment is also unexecuted and names two different issuing companies.
4. **Seller affidavit contradicted at nine points** — taxes, mechanic's lien, federal tax lien, judgment, lis pendens, TCEQ notice, SNDA status, lease-term sufficiency and boundary matters — plus it cites a survey by a different firm, misstates deed types and acquisition dates, and omits all five adverse items from what it calls a "complete accounting".
5. **Ten of 78 turbines** (12.8%) sit inside a recorded prohibition or a physical conflict: conservation easement (T-65/66/67), covenants (T-30/31, T-68/69), CPS transmission corridor (T-14/15) and FEMA Zone AE (T-42).
6. **Senior lessor debt with no SNDA** on 1,260 acres, and a live forgery challenge to 560–640 acres of leasehold.
7. **Monetary exposure recomputed:** $12,361,376 at 1 April 2025 rising to $12,592,209 by 1 October 2025, plus a contingent $2,415,000 lessor payoff and unquantified rollback tax.

## Report structure

Executive summary with 14 red flags → scope and sources → transaction and title structure → acreage verification → the encumbrance register (monetary, title/litigation, leases, 26 easements, land-use controls, mineral, regulatory) → survey conflicts and documentation defects → affidavit reconciliation (18 representations tested) → 51-item cross-document inconsistency log → 30-item consents and closing-condition matrix → financial summary and prorations → risk register and conditions precedent → 22 diligence requests → appendices (source register, 47-parcel matrix, 63-item index, computations and dates, qualifications).

All computations flagged [verified] are reproducible from the source figures; inferences are marked [inference]. No recorded instrument was examined — every recording reference is reproduced as stated by the source — and that limitation is stated in Section 2.3 and Appendix E.
"}
